Through the fixed place, one receives the power of the eating- birur from the fixed place of Torah — which derives from the fixed place of the Aron that Dovid found, where the eating- birur reaches its perfection: "you shall eat there before Hashem your G-d." All eating everywhere draws its birur -power from there = Birchas HaMazon blessing Eretz Yisrael . One person exem

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Betzias HaPas Intro 9-10
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Betzias Hapas Intro Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Betzias HaPas — Introductory Sections (§§ 9–10) COMPLETE FULL TRANSLATION Continuation of Netilas Yadayim material · Based on LM II:7 § 9 — The Five Species of Grain, the Hai of HaShishi , and Mezona D'Nishmasa Therefore they are the five species [of grain]. Corresponding to the Hai of HaShishi [the sixth day — in the Torah, the sixth day of creation uniquely has the article Hai : " yom ha shishi "]. For the entire world was suspended until the sixth of Sivan, when Israel received the Torah, which is the aspect of nevu'ah [prophecy], through which the renewal of the world was revealed, as explained in the aforementioned Torah [of Rabbainu]. It emerges that the Hai of HaShishi signifies the renewal of the world. And from there is the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael , which receives its holiness through "the power of His deeds," etc. — through knowing that Hashem created the world, the aspect of "In the beginning [He] created," etc., as explained in the aforementioned Torah . And from there — from the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , from the aspect of the renewal of the world that was revealed through the Hai of HaShishi — from there we receive the aspect of the five species [of grain], which are the praise of Eretz Yisrael . For the five species correspond to the Hai of HaShishi , through which the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael [is drawn]. From there the five species receive their power to nourish and satiate a person in the aspect of mezona d'nishmasa [nourishment of the soul], from which the essential true satiation derives, in the aspect of "the tzadik eats to satisfy his soul." Therefore specifically the five species have the power to satiate a person, for they receive their power from Eretz Yisrael , from the aspect of the Hai of HaShishi , from the aspect of the faith in the renewal of the world, from which mezona d'nishmasa is drawn — from which the essential satiation [comes]. For in mezona d'gufa [nourishment of the body], which is the aspect of Eisav's eating, eating of the Sitra Achra , it is said: "the belly of the wicked shall be wanting." But mezona d'nishmasa — there is the essential satiation, in the aspect of "the tzadik eats to satisfy his soul." For mezona d'nishmasa is the aspect of "Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack," the aspect of "there is no lack for those who fear Him," as explained in the aforementioned Torah — the opposite of mezona d'gufa , which is the aspect of the eating of the wicked, which is the aspect of "the belly of the wicked shall be wanting," as above. Therefore also in the physical [realm], the essential satiation is through the five species, which are the primary bread that sustains the heart, upon which one is obligated to say HaMotzi and Birchas HaMazon . For they are the five species — the praise of Eretz Yisrael — into which the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is drawn, the aspect of the faith in the renewal of the world that was revealed through the Hai of HaShishi , on account of which they are five species, as above. And through their being in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , etc. — through this they are in the aspect of mezona d'nishmasa even more. Therefore the essential satiation is through them, as above. This is the aspect of the Hai of HaMotzi . One must enunciate the Hai of " HaMotzi ," as our Sages zichronam livrachah cautioned, and the holy Zohar speaks at great length about the matter of the Hai of HaMotzi . For the Hai of " Ha Motzi " is the aspect of the Hai of " Ha Shishi ," which signifies the renewal of the world — through which the essential tikkun of holy eating in the aspect of mezona d'nishmasa [is achieved], as above. And this is why our Sages zichronam livrachah linked the blessing of HaMotzi with the Hai to the verse: " Ha Motzi eschem mi'tachas sivlos Mitzrayim" — "Who brings you out from under the burdens of Mitzrayim." For in truth it is all one and the same. For the verse "Who brings you out from under the burdens of Mitzrayim" — i.e. the Exodus from Mitzrayim — signifies the renewal of the world. For at the time of the Exodus, the renewal of the world was revealed through the signs and wonders, as is brought in all the holy books. Moreover, the essential purpose of the Exodus was for the sake of receiving the Torah, as it is written: "when you bring the nation out of Mitzrayim, you shall serve [G-d on this mountain]," etc. And the essential revelation of the renewal of the world was through the receiving of the Torah, as above. It emerges that the verse "Who brings you out from under the burdens of Mitzrayim" signifies the renewal of the world. Therefore from there our Sages zichronam livrachah derived the Hai of HaMotzi — which is the essential tikkun — which signifies the renewal of the world, which is the essential tikkun of eating in the aspect of mezona d'nishmasa , as above. § 10 — Blessing Over a Whole Loaf And this is why on

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Betzias HaPas Part2 22-31
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 2: §§ 22–31) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — continuation. § 22 — Karpas : The Eating of Humility And this is the aspect of karpas — a type of vegetable that we eat then — which is the aspect of mochin d'katnus [constricted consciousness]. It hints that even though we drank the first cup, we have not yet merited to eat the matzah , which is the food of angels in the aspect of the man [manna], as our Sages say. Rather, we must first remember our lowliness. For now, before the giving of the Torah, before is'arusa d'l'sata , our eating is in the aspect of animal food — the aspect of "you shall eat the grass of the field" (Genesis 3:18) — because [Adam] blemished through eating from the Tree of Knowledge. As our Sages say: when Hashem said to Adam HaRishon "you shall eat the grass of the field," he trembled — until [Hashem] said to him: "By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread" — hinting that through the exertions of Israel in Torah and mitzvos , they will merit the eating of bread, which is human food. § 23 — Yachatz : Breaking Before Telling And this is the aspect of Yachatz — breaking the matzah — to indicate that even though we break and divide it, it is impossible to eat immediately until we tell of the Exodus to include the worlds. And then we merit the eating of matzah , which is the aspect of silence regarding the kushyos — only we respond with many words of songs and praises for having taken us out of Egypt and revealed His G-dliness before our eyes. This is the aspect of lechem oni [bread of poverty / bread upon which we answer] — as explained in the Hilchos Pesach. And see above (§§11–12) regarding betzi'as hapas — that the main thing is to break with a berachah properly so as to draw the illumination of Ratzon during eating. But now on Pesach, which is the beginning of the drawing close — one cannot eat immediately. Therefore we break and shatter the matzah beforehand — this is Yachatz — and do not eat until the Haggadah is recited: to indicate that now it is impossible to draw the tikkun of the breaking (the illumination of Ratzon ) except through the telling of the Exodus, through which the worlds are included together. § 24 — The Last Two Cups: The Two Hands And afterward, one drinks two more cups — which correspond to the two hands in yam hachochmah , which are the remazim from which sustenance and eating [derive], and from which the illumination of Ratzon [is drawn]. And the overall structure of the four cups corresponds to the Malchus that ascends to receive sustenance from the two hands in yam hachochmah . This constitutes four aspects: Chochmah , Malchus , and the two hands — through which the illumination of Ratzon shines in completeness. Therefore we conclude with Nirtzah — the aspect of the illumination of Ratzon , in the wondrous tikkunim that we merit through the entire Seder. § 25 — The Cups Are Yirah And the cups themselves in which the wine of the four cups is drunk are the aspect of yirah . For kos [cup] in gematria equals Elokim , which is the aspect of yirah — "I fear G-d" (Genesis 42:18) . For all the aspects mentioned above are included in yirah , which is the aspect of Malchus , as explained in the Torah teaching. Therefore the drinking of wine is called by the name of the cups — for the wine, which is the drawing of Ratzon , cannot be drawn and received except through yirah , the Malchus that ascends and receives sustenance from yam hachochmah . And all the illumination of son and student is likewise in the aspect of yirah , as explained there. § 26 — The Two Washings: Bitachon And this is the aspect of the two washings on the night of Pesach. Rechitzah [washing] is the aspect of bitachon [trust], for bitachon in the Targum's language is rechitzah . Before eating, one must wash his hands in water — this is the mitzvah of netilas yadayim for a meal — to purify the hands, which are "busy" [in the affairs of the world], so that one can draw the flow of sustenance from the hands in yam hachochmah . All of this is drawn through bitachon , as explained in the Torah teaching: all look expectantly for sustenance, and the Malchus collects all these trusts and ascends with them to receive sustenance from the hands in yam hachochmah . Therefore one needs rechitzah in water before eating — for the water, which is the da'as of yam hachochmah , purifies from all impurities that come through the ruach shtus [spirit of folly], the opposite of da'as . And for the most part, the ruach shtus prevents one from serving Hashem through the anxiety of livelihood — the ruach shtus deceives him as if it is in the power of his hands to draw sustenance, which is the blemish of: "And you say: my power and the might of my hand made me this wealth" (Deuteronomy 8:17) . Therefore one washes his hands in water — to indicate that sustenance comes on

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Betzias HaPas Part3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 3: §§ 32–43) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — continuation. § 32 — Barley to Wheat: Rectifying Adam's Sin Through Eating Further explanation is needed here. For initially one must rectify the aspect of animal food — the Omer of barley. And afterward, on Shavuos , one merits the two loaves of wheat — human food. This is the rectification of the sin of Adam HaRishon, to whom it was first said: "you shall eat the grass of the field" — animal food, as our Sages say: he trembled and said, "I and the donkey at one trough?" And afterward [Hashem] said to him: "By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread." This is the aspect of eating karpas on Pesach before the Seder begins — a type of vegetable — and afterward eating matzah . For the essential tikkun is to merit the illumination of Ratzon during eating, drawn from the aspect of silence — "one does not converse during a meal." § 33 — The Wondrous Unity of the Torah Teaching For the Torah teaching "Ki Merachamam" (and indeed all the Torah teachings) is bound together in a wondrous knot . For at first it wrote that one must illuminate the holy da'as in every person — this is the essential compassion — to extract him from sins that come through ruach shtus . Then it revealed further that the tzadik illuminates in the upper and lower dwellers — informing those lying in the lowest depths, in the lowest pit of She'ol and below it, that even there Hashem is still with them, for "the whole earth is full of His glory" — and awakening them in the aspect of "awaken and sing, dwellers of the dust." In truth, it is all one matter. For through this itself — that [the tzadik ] has the power to inform the lower ones, even the exceedingly fallen, that Hashem is still with them — through this itself he illuminates in them the da'as and drives away the ruach shtus each time. For it is certainly a great labor and exceedingly wondrous craft to illuminate da'as in such people who have stumbled in sins — especially those who stumbled deliberately in tremendous sins, may the Merciful One save us. Yet the tzadik is such a compassionate one that even in them he illuminates the holy da'as through his goodness and mercy. For through his great power, he informs them that Hashem is still with them , that "there is no place empty of Him." Through this itself, the ruach shtus is driven away each time. For even if a person is however he is — the moment he is informed that Hashem is found even there, as it is written: "Who dwells with them in the midst of their impurity" (Leviticus 16:16) — for even in the ten crowns of impurity Hashem is found, since all their vitality is from Him alone — immediately the ruach shtus flees, in the aspect of: "the idols of Egypt tremble before Him" (Isaiah 19:1) , and: "I shall pass through the land of Egypt — and I shall be revealed… I am Hashem, and not an angel" — and then: "I shall smite every firstborn" — which is the da'as of the sitra achra , from which the ruach shtus [derives]. For who would dare approach Him? All of this is the aspect of offering the Omer of barley — animal food, the ruach shtus — that the tzadik , the aspect of Moshe, with his great power can elevate even the barley, animal food, ruach shtus — sifting it through thirteen sieves until he refines even from there holy and wondrous sparks, until everything ascends as a pleasing fragrance to Hashem. For within the animalistic itself, within the ruach shtus itself, His G-dly vitality is hidden — sustaining them all. Therefore, through waving the Omer of barley and offering it to Hashem, one reveals that even in all the lowest levels where all the stragglers and fallen have descended — even there Hashem is found , for "the whole earth is full of His glory." Therefore we immediately begin counting the days for the Omer . For every day contains wisdom and da'as , the aspect of "days shall speak" (Job 32:7) . Now, through the mitzvah of counting, we bind each day to the Omer — to exit thereby from the contamination of Egypt. For by binding the days to the Omer , we reveal that even within the contamination of Egypt itself, within the ruach shtus itself, Hashem is hidden. Through this itself, the contamination — the ruach shtus — flees. For through the counting, we bind time and the days to the aspect of above time — tekufos hayamim — which are the secret of the makifin drawn through the counting. This is the inclusiveness of the lower in the upper — for there, in the aspect of the upper, it is above time. Time exists only in the aspect of the lower, where there is counting and number. For "before the One, what do you count?" — but we, the children of Israel, through the power of the true tzadikim in every generation who are the aspect of Moshe, bind through the counting the days and time to the aspect of above time — the inclusiveness of the

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 2 COMPLETE · Based on LM I:7 ( V'Aileh HaMishpatim ) Shulchan Aruch text: Four are obligated to give thanks: a sick person who was healed, those who go down to the sea, etc., travelers through wildernesses, and one who was imprisoned. The mnemonic is: "and all who live [v'chol ha' ch a' y ' i ' m '] shall thank You" etc. (Shulchan Aruch, siman 219). Emunah = Miracles = Tefilah = Eretz Yisrael Based on the teaching " V'Aileh HaMishpatim " which discusses emunah ( LM I:7 ); see there. For emunah is the aspect of tefilah , the aspect of miracles — that one believes there is One who renews and in whose hand it is to change nature. The essential tefilah , the aspect of emunah , the aspect of miracles — is only in Eretz Yisrael , etc. Therefore, when Avraham damaged in Eretz Yisrael by saying "how shall I know?" — through this, Yaakov and his sons descended into the exile of Egypt. For the essential exile is because of the deficiency of emunah , etc. The essential ge'ulah [redemption] is through emunah , in the aspect of: "you shall come, you shall gaze from the peak of Amanah" etc. (Shir HaShirim 4). But to merit emunah , one must attain truth — for "when tzedek joins with emes , it becomes emunah ." The essential truth is merited only through drawing close to true tzadikim — by receiving their counsel, for they are the aspect of "a faithful offspring — entirely seed of truth," the aspect of the 613 counsels of the Torah, etc. Through the mitzvah of tzitzis , one merits being saved from the counsel of the wicked, which is the aspect of adultery, etc. — for tzitzis is a protection from adultery. Therefore through tzitzis one merits receiving counsel from the tzadikim , who are the aspect of guarding the bris , the aspect of "a faithful offspring — entirely seed of truth." Through this one merits emunah , as mentioned above. Through this the ge'ulah will come, etc., as above; see there. The Four Who Give Thanks Reveal Emunah and Defeat the Four Exiles This is the aspect of Birchas HaHodaos HaNissim [blessings of thanksgiving for miracles]. One must give thanks and bless Hashem for the miracles — in order to reveal emunah in the world, to know and make known that Hashem governs the world and in His mercy changed nature and performed a miracle for him. This is the essential aspect of emunah , as above. For miracles, the aspect of tefilah , are the aspect of emunah , as above. This is the aspect of the four who must give thanks. When a miracle is performed and one thanks Hashem for it — and through this emunah , the aspect of tefilah , is revealed, as above — through this the ge'ulah will come and one merits leaving the exile of the four kingdoms. For the essential exile is because of the deficiency of emunah , as above. Therefore they are four who must give thanks — corresponding to the four exiles. For through the four who must give thanks, all four exiles are subdued and nullified. For the essential exile is through the deficiency of emunah , as above. Through the four who must give thanks — through the thanksgiving for miracles — emunah is revealed, as above, through which the ge'ulah will come, as above. For emunah is the aspect of the daled of "Echad" [in Krias Shma ]. Therefore the essential emunah is through the tzadik , who is the aspect of truth, as above. For the tzadik is the kotz [serif] of the letter daled , as brought in the Tikunim (Tikun 21, daf 55b). The essential sustaining of emunah — which is the daled of "Echad" — is through the tzadik , who is the aspect of "a faithful offspring — entirely seed of truth," as above. Therefore the tzadik is the kotz of the letter daled , as above. This is the aspect of the four tzitzis , through which one merits drawing close to the tzadik and meriting emunah , as above. Through the four tzitzis , one merits the closeness of the tzadik — who is the kotz of the letter daled , the aspect of "a faithful offspring — entirely seed of truth" — through whom the essential sustaining of emunah is accomplished, as above. Through emunah , one merits ge'ulah and leaves the four exiles, as above. This is the aspect of the four who must give thanks — four specifically, as above. Yetzias Mitzrayim: All Four in One For all the four who must give thanks are in the aspect of Yetzias Mitzrayim . The exile of Egypt came about through the damage of emunah , as above, in the above teaching; see there. Likewise all four exiles are called by the name "Mitzrayim," and they all come through the damage of emunah , as above. Yetzias Mitzrayim — the aspect of miracles, the aspect of tefilah , emunah — this is the aspect of the four who must give thanks. Through the thanksgiving, the aspect of tefilah , one publicizes and reveals the miracle, the aspect of emunah , as above. This is the aspect of Yetzias Mitzrayim — for the essential ge'

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 5 Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 5 Part 1 (Intro + §§ 1–8 / Oaseyos א–ח) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:31 ( Ais Lan Bira B'Davra ) Shulchan Aruch text: Four must give thanks: sea-travelers, wilderness-travelers, etc., a sick person who was healed, and one who was imprisoned and released. The mnemonic: "and all who live [v'chol ha' ch a' y ' i ' m '] shall thank You" etc. Introduction: Letters, Vowel-Points, Longings, and the Four Tikunim Based on the Torah " Ais lan bira b'davra " ( LM I:31 ); see there. The principle is: tzedakah governs all the celestial spheres, etc. All the sufferings a person has on his journeys are due to the celestial spheres, etc. — for there are stars that decree there shall be a road, etc., and stars that decree there shall be a wilderness, etc. Therefore the remedy for this is to give tzedakah before going on a journey, as it says: "righteousness shall go before him and shall direct his steps on the way" etc. The essential completeness of the spheres — the completeness of tzedakah — is only through Shabbos , etc., which is the aspect of emunah . The essential sustaining of emunah is through the aspect of bris , etc. There are two aspects of bris : the aspect of Avraham, which is bris ilah [the upper covenant] — the firmament that separates between the upper waters and the lower waters; and the aspect of Eliezer, which is bris tata'ah [the lower covenant] — the aspect of Chanoch- Metat , etc. This is the firmament that separates between clean waters and impure waters, between forbidden and permitted, etc. Bris ilah is guarding the holy bris . Bris tata'ah is guarding forbidden and permitted, etc. A person must have both aspects of bris — he must be both a tzadik and a lamdan [Torah scholar], etc. Through this one merits the aspect of chesed — love and yearning for Hashem — and then he makes souls: he makes vowel-points for the letters of the Torah. For letters without vowel-points are like a body without a soul — they have no movement or function without a soul. So too, the combining and pairing of the letters through the 231 Gates to produce some action — they have no power except according to the vowel-points. The vowel-points are the love and longings, in the aspect of nekudos hakesef [points of silver = points of longing]. The longings are the soul, etc. According to the longings, so are the vowel-points: if one longs for evil, he makes evil vowel-points, and then the letters combine and pair to produce evil actions. If one longs to return in teshuvah , good vowel-points are made — good souls — and the letters move and pair to produce good actions, etc. This is: "if the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem Tz'vakos" — he must be both a tzadik and a lamdan , etc.; see all this there well. See what pertains to this, printed nearby, in my [Reb Noson's] own words. The principle is: the longings and yearning for something holy are exceedingly precious. Through them a good soul is formed and completed through speech, and it goes forth and transmigrates. Sometimes the soul of holiness transmigrates into a wicked person and thoughts of teshuvah fall upon him, and he can be brought back to good. And conversely, chas v'shalom , how much evil is caused by longing for something evil, chas v'shalom — the soul formed through evil longings sometimes transmigrates into a tzadik and can cause him to sin, chas v'shalom . This is: "there is a vanity that is done on the earth" etc.; see all this there well. See there regarding the four who entered the Pardais [orchard], etc. He explains there that one who separates a lamdan from a tzadik — who says that being a lamdan alone is a virtue — is in the aspect of Acher who "cut the plantings," who separated the aspect of Metat , the aspect of an angel — the aspect of a lamdan , the aspect of kasher and pasul [permitted and forbidden] — from "Hashem Tz'vakos" — the aspect of a tzadik with good deeds. For in truth, a lamdan — even in Torah — without good deeds is nothing. On the contrary: "if he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death for him." Therefore the teacher must resemble an angel of "Hashem Tz'vakos" — he is a lamdan in Torah and serves Hashem with righteousness and good deeds. Through this he forms the letters of the Torah for good — then "Torah shall be sought from his mouth" : the letters of the Torah seek to receive vowel-points and be formed from his mouth. Through his mouth speaking his holy yearnings and longings, the souls (= vowel-points for the letters) go forth, and the letters are formed and paired for good, etc. For the letters of the Torah are active agents — they are the vitality of everything and govern the world. Everything depends on the vowel-points that people draw through their longings for good or the reverse, chas v'shalom — through which the letters are formed for good or the reverse. Therefore

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 5 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 5 Part 2 (§§ 9–15 / Oaseyos ט–טו) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:31 ( Ais Lan Bira B'Davra ) § 9 — Korach Swallowed Alive: Separating Letters from Vowel-Points = Death Therefore Korach and his assembly were swallowed alive, as it says: "they descended alive to the pit." The essential death derives from the above-mentioned damage — by not forming the letters of the Torah for good, which is the aspect of "if he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death." This damage derives essentially from not drawing close to the true tzadik — all the more when one disputes him, chas v'shalom , and separates lamdan from tzadik : separating Torah-study from good longings (= good souls, good vowel-points), as above. Through this, "if he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death" — since he separates the letters of Torah from the vowel-points, which is literally the departure of the soul from the body: the essential death, as above. The essential death derives from the sin of Adam HaRishon through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. The essential damage of the Tree of Knowledge was this very aspect. The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil is the aspect of Metat , encompassing the six orders of Mishnah — the aspect of forbidden and permitted, etc. — as known in the Tikunim. Hashem commanded him not to eat from the Tree of Knowledge at all — He wanted him to cleave only to the Tree of Life, which is entirely good, and then no sorting would have been needed at all. But he sinned and ate from the Tree of Knowledge through the counsel of the serpent, who was more cunning than all, enticing him to become clever: "your eyes will be opened" etc. — enticing him to pursue only wisdoms and investigations, to know good and evil, without striving after good deeds at all. Until the serpent overpowered him and enticed him to violate Hashem's command, to eat from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. He also damaged the holy bris , as our Sages say. Through all this he was in the aspect of "a gossip separates a chief" — he separated lamdan from tzadik , like Acher who "cut the plantings," as above. For through eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil and through damaging the bris , he caused a separation between the aspect of lamdan (= the six orders of Mishnah, Metat -angel) and the aspect of tzadik (= guarding the bris , "Hashem Tz'vakos" ), as above. This is the separation of the letters from the vowel-points — the aspect of body and soul. Therefore death was decreed through this — the departure of the soul from the body — for he damaged by separating the vowel-points from the letters, which is literally the departure of the soul from the body, as above. But Adam HaRishon did teshuvah and began to rectify somewhat. Likewise all the tzadikim in every generation work on this tikun . The essential tikun is through true tzadikim who overcame their inclination until they merited tikun habris in truth — through which they merited good longings and making good vowel-points for the letters, through which everything is formed for good: the aspect of life, the aspect of "if he merited, it becomes a potion of life," as above. Whoever wants to protect his life must bind himself to true tzadikim , for with them is the source of life, as above. In every generation they work to rectify the sin of Adam HaRishon through the true tzadikim and those who draw close to them — through which lamdan and tzadik are included together, vowel-points and letters, Torah and good deeds, the encompassing of body within soul: the aspect of life, as above. Nevertheless, since this tikun cannot be completed all at once or in a single generation, the decree of death remains in place and ultimately a person must die. Due to the enormity of the damage of Adam HaRishon's sin, the contamination can only be sorted through the departure of the soul from the body. But in truth, now death is a great good, as it says: "and behold, it was very good — this is death," as our Sages say. For now, after the sin, even great tzadikim cannot return to the source of life in completeness except through the departure of the soul from the body — when "the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to G-d who gave it." Then the contamination of the body decomposes in the dust until, at the time of the Resurrection, the soul and the purified body will reunite and arise in the Resurrection, living true life — eternal life — each according to the good deeds he merited accumulating in this world, and according to his closeness and attachment to true tzadikim and yir'aim , through which he worked to unite soul and body, as above. Through this he will ultimately merit this union in completeness — eternal life, as above. But it is impossible to reach eternal life except through death specifically — so th

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 1 (§§ 1–10 / Oaseyos א–י) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 1 — Performing the Mitzvah with Joy: The Nine Chambers Based on the Torah " Amtza'isa d'alma " ( LM I:24 ). He explains there the supreme virtue of performing the mitzvah with joy — through which one merits raising the Shechinah from her exile, etc., ascending ever higher until one merits grasping the light of the Ain Sof in the aspect of mati v'lo mati [reaching and not reaching]. This light is above nefesh, ruach, neshamah , etc.; see all this there very well. Especially what he explains regarding the nine chambers that are not illuminated, etc. — which are fashioned through the tikunim and ascents merited through performing the mitzvah with joy. One ascends ever higher until the Arranger and Settler of the mental faculties is blessed — the aspect of Keser , etc. Then through the pursuit and the obstructer, the mental faculties are struck by the Settler and Arranger, and the nine chambers that are not illuminated are fashioned, etc. — "none can stand within them, they do not cling and are not known" etc.; see there. You, the student, must know and believe that everything stated there is accomplished through every single Jew when he merits strengthening himself to perform the mitzvah with joy. For "it is not in heaven" — the Torah was not given to those who ascend to heaven, etc. — for "the matter is very close to us" etc. This is not the place to elaborate on this. § 2 — The Obligation of Thanksgiving: Joy Rectifies the Exile of the Shechinah This is the aspect of the obligation of thanksgiving upon all who emerge from distress — the four who must give thanks: wilderness-travelers, etc., those released from prison, the sick who are healed, and sea-travelers when they come up from there. All troubles, Rachmana litzlan , are the aspect of the exile of the Shechinah — for "in all their affliction, He is afflicted," as is known. The essential exile of the Shechinah is the overpowering of sadness upon the hearts of Israel, in the aspect of "He was grieved in His heart," as explained in the above Torah . From there come all the desires — particularly the desire for relations and the desire for money — which come only from sadness. From there all troubles come, Rachmana litzlan . Therefore, when Hashem helps and one emerges from the distress, one must bring a korban Todah [thanksgiving-offering]. Now, when we have no korban , one must give thanks verbally with all his heart — which is the aspect of joy. For the essential joy is thanksgiving to Hashem — the essential ultimate joy of the future, when we will engage only in todah and thanksgiving to Hashem with immense joy: "give thanks to Hashem with the harp; with the ten-stringed lyre sing to Him" — the aspect of the ten types of melody. As it says: "a psalm for thanksgiving: call out to Hashem, all the earth; serve Hashem with joy" etc. This is the essential tikun of the todah and thanksgiving one is obligated to give when emerging from distress — to rectify the damage from which the troubles came, which is the sadness, as above. So that henceforth we merit being saved from all troubles through the intensity of joy — until we merit all the above tikunim , grasping the above-mentioned light, the essential purpose, as explained there. Therefore "all the korbanos will be nullified except the korban Todah" (Midrash Rabbah, Vayikra, Parshah 27). § 3 — The Four Types of Bread: Ten Loaves = Ten Types of Melody For this reason one brings in the korban Todah four types of bread, each consisting of ten loaves. The essential sadness clings to the bread, in the aspect of: "in sadness you shall eat it"; "by the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread." Conversely, the essential tikun of eating is through joy: "eat your bread in joy," in the aspect of "eating and drinking and rejoicing" etc. Therefore there are ten loaves of each type — corresponding to the ten types of melody, which are the source and totality of all joys. § 4 — The Four Types of Bread in Detail: The Tikunim of the Todah One can also allude, in specific detail, to the four types of bread brought in the korban Todah : they correspond to the tikunim fashioned through the joy of the mitzvah , which is the aspect of the korban Todah , as above. As explained in the above Torah : through the joy of the mitzvah , Malchus rises from among the klipos . When a person performs a mitzvah , the mitzvah has the power to go and arouse all the worlds to serve Hashem, etc. This is the aspect of Malchus clothing Netzach-Hod-Yesod , the instruments of walking, etc. Through the walking, blessing is drawn to all the worlds. This is the aspect of Netzach-Hod-Yesod clothing Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes — the hands, from which all blessings come, etc. The essential blessing flowing from the hand

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 2 (§§ 11–23 / Oaseyos יא–כג) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 11 — Mizmor Hodu on Erev Shabbos: Drawing Shabbos-Joy into the Weekdays Therefore, upon entering Shabbos — when one must pass from the mundane to Shabbos , from the bitterness of troubles and exile clinging to the six weekdays, to merit the holiness of Shabbos (= freedom) — we recite Mizmor " Hodu ," which discusses the four who must give thanks. The purpose is to draw upon oneself the joy of thanksgiving from the aspect of Shabbos , the World to Come, so that through this we merit leaving the exile of the six weekdays and attaining the holiness of Shabbos (= freedom). The essential freedom is through joy: "for with joy you shall go out." One depends on the other: the more the exile overpowers, chas v'shalom , the more sadness overpowers — the essential exile is sadness overpowering the hearts of Israel, not allowing them to rejoice. The more sadness overpowers, the more exile overpowers, as above. Therefore one must overpower to gladden his soul through all kinds of counsel, as explained in Rabbainu's words zichrono livrachah . Therefore one must constantly remind himself of the holiness of Shabbos , the world of freedom, in order to draw Shabbos -joy into the weekdays, as explained elsewhere. This is the aspect of "from the first day of the week toward Shabbos" — one must draw upon himself Shabbos -joy even during the weekdays, as above. This is the aspect of the Song of the Day, where we specifically mention Shabbos every single day: "Today is the first day toward Shabbos ; today is the second day toward Shabbos ," etc. Then we recite the Song of the Day that was recited in the Bais HaMikdash . For song is the aspect of joy — we remind ourselves of the holiness of Shabbos , which is the aspect of song, thanksgiving, and joy. The essential song and thanksgiving (= joy) is on Shabbos : "a psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos; it is good to give thanks to Hashem... upon the ten-stringed... for You have gladdened me, Hashem, with Your works" etc. From there all the songs the Levi'im would recite in the Bais HaMikdash every day are drawn. Therefore we mention Shabbos specifically alongside the Song of the Day — to draw Shabbos -joy into each day. Then we recite the song the Levi'im would say in the Bais HaMikdash — all in the above aspect: we recall even now the song of the Bais HaMikdash (= joy), all to draw from the aspect of Shabbos , from the ultimate end when the Bais HaMikdash will be rebuilt and joy will be immense. Through this we gladden ourselves even now with this hope — for in the end of all ends everything will be rectified, sins will be transformed to merits, everything will turn to good, as above. All this he hinted in his answer: "aisu ashli u'moshchu" etc. — reminding them of the great joy of the future, through which we can gladden ourselves even now, as above. Through this we merit leaving the Chambers of Exchange they mentioned there, alluded to in the question "mi yaimar" etc., as explained there. § 12 — The Chambers of Exchange: How the Sitra Achra Reverses Everything The Sitra Achra and the klipos — the forces of the yetzer hara and his armies — are called the Chambers of Exchange. Their entire evil power is through exchanges: swapping evil for good and good for evil, in the aspect of: "woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness into light and light into darkness" etc. (Yeshayah 5). From there come all the confusions, all the desires, all types of dispute, enticements, seductions, and false reasonings, etc. The essential thing is through sadness — through which the mind and intellect become confused, as explained in the above-mentioned Torah ( LM II:10 ). The essential confusion is that they confuse the da'as , exchanging and reversing everything: "your reversal" (Yeshayah 29); "they rebelled and grieved His holy spirit" (Yeshayah 63). All language of rebellion and defiance ( sorer u'moreh ) is on account of the exchanges, from which many are brought to actual bitterness, Rachmana litzlan : "today it tells him 'do this,' tomorrow it tells him 'do that,' until..." etc. — all through false reasonings and exchanges. Therefore it was established in many prayers and confessions from the early ones to say: "What You made stringent, I treated lightly; what You treated lightly, I made stringent; what You forbade, I permitted; what You permitted, I forbade" — and much more (as brought in the confession of Tikun Erev Rosh Chodesh ). Even their stringencies cause much harm, and likewise their mitzvos — for usually the ba'al davar [adversary] garbs himself in mitzvos (as brought in LM I:1 ). All this is the aspect of exchanges and reversals. This is the aspect of fallen fears, Rachmana litzlan . One should fear only Hashem alone: "

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 3 (§§ 24–36 / Oaseyos כד–לו) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 24 — Yaakov's Dream at Bais Kel: The Ladder, the Stone, and the Obstructer "He encountered the place" — the aspect of the striking of the pursuit against the obstructer, the aspect of Keser , called "place," as explained in the above Torah on the verse "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place." From there is the essential root of all places in the world, drawn forth and coming into being through many tzimtzumim . This is the aspect of what is explained ( LM II:83 ): the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know — the aspect of "the Place of the world," etc.; see there. "He lodged there, for the sun had set" — the setting of the sun is the aspect of the withdrawal and prevention of the light through the obstructer. The sun is the light of intellect pursuing to grasp the light, but the obstructer prevents it, as above. Therefore "he lodged there" — the essential sleep is this aspect. By day, through tefilah , Torah, and mitzvos with joy, the mental faculties are drawn through the striking of the pursuit against the obstructer, etc. But from the exertion they must withdraw after tefilah — only a residual impression remains. Afterward, toward evening, they withdraw completely, as explained in the kavanos of the Arizal. This is: "he lodged there, for the sun had set" — Yaakov saw it was impossible now to perceive the mental faculties in completeness, for the sorting from the Chambers of Exchange had not yet been completed. Therefore "he lodged there." "He lodged there" also alludes to the exiles, as our Sages say. From there all exiles come — through the corruptions of the generations who do not properly sort from the Chambers of Exchange, many causing damage, Rachmana litzlan . Because of this, even the great tzadikim , the forefathers, cannot perceive as they wish. Therefore he was compelled to lodge — the aspect of sleep and cessation — until he sorts properly. This is: "one who comes to purify is told: wait!" — said regarding every Jew wanting to purify himself, as explained ( LM I:6 ). And likewise regarding the tzadik laboring to purify Israel. "He took from the stones of the place and set them at his head" — he took and sorted from the stones of the place: the sorting of letters and sparks — holy stones fallen into the Chambers of Exchange (= stumbling-stones): "the holy stones are poured out" etc. The tzadik sorts the good stones (= holy stones, the letters of Torah) from the Chambers of Exchange, and "set them at his head" — binding them into the head and intellect. "He lay down in that place" — he fell asleep amidst words of Torah. This alludes to every person: when one sees he is being prevented as he is being prevented, he must bind words of Torah in his thought, remove his thought from evil musings, and bind words of Torah in his thought until he falls asleep amidst words of Torah — the essential sorting from the Chambers of Exchange. This is the aspect of teshuvah of corresponding weight — the essential tikun of the damage of the bris (= the damage of thought), whose entire tikun is specifically through this, as brought regarding the teaching of our Sages (in LM I:27 , the Torah " R'tzitzah "; see there). This is: "he lay down in that place" — "that place" specifically, where he encountered (= the obstructer). There specifically he bound his thought with a strong bond until he slept. Every person must do likewise: even though he sees his thought is being obstructed as it is obstructed, he must do his part — to flee from evil thoughts and bind his thought to the aspect of "the Place of the world." Even though he cannot yet perceive or understand anything from there, his thought should remain bound there through the stones of the place (= the letters of Torah), until he falls asleep amidst words of Torah — the aspect of "he lay down in that place," as above. "He dreamt, and behold, a ladder set upon the earth, its top reaching the heavens" etc. He saw this is the totality of man's service in this world: one must descend to this physical earth where the Chambers of Exchange cling, sort from there, and ascend through all the above ascents by means of this ladder whose top reaches the heavens — the aspect of the upper Prisah (= Keser ), through which all perception of the nine chambers is accomplished, as above. Sulam [ladder] alludes to this, for sulam in gematria equals kol [voice] — the aspect of "the voice is the voice of Yaakov." Through this comes all the Jew's overpowering against all the Sitra Achra and Chambers of Exchange, all encompassed in Esav: "when the voice is the voice of Yaakov, the hands are not the hands of Esav" — he has no power. "The voice is the voice of Yaakov" — two voices. The essential completeness is joy, through which all

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part4
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 4 (§§ 37–50 / Oaseyos לז–נ) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 37 — Notzair [Guards] = Ratzon [Will]: The Inflaming of Truth Through Desire Notzair [guards/preserves] is the letters of ratzon [will] — for the essential thing is the will, as explained in our writings extensively. This is the essential illumination of the inflaming of truth in the heart: the truth should illuminate and inflame in his heart always, in gradation and measure, until his will is strong always for Hashem, His Torah, and His true tzadikim — this is the essential thing, as above. Therefore, when one reaches the aspect of Notzair Chesed [the eighth of the thirteen midos of mercy], no further open kindling is needed, as above — one cannot illuminate further in the open. The essential tikun is through the strong will, which shines even more through the inflaming of truth — the aspect of Yosef, as above. § 38 — Yosef's True Dreams and Interpreting Others' Dreams: Sleep, Sadness, and Exile Therefore Yosef the tzadik merited true and accurate dreams, and also knew how to interpret the dreams of others during their sleep. Sleep is one-sixtieth of death, and sadness is the side of death. The essential sleep comes from the wearying of the mind. The root of holy sleep (= the sleep of the tzadikim ) derives from the pursuit and obstructer: the mind pursues to perceive, the obstructer obstructs until it settles, etc. — through which the nine chambers are fashioned, and one perceives the Ain Sof light. Even though these nine chambers do not cling and are not known — from there all the holy mental faculties of the true tzadikim derive, for they are the lights of the tzachtzachos [brilliant splendors] — the root of all the midos , from which all mental faculties descend through the tzimtzumim and vessels the tzadikim fashion through their good deeds. However, due to the wearying of the mind through the pursuit and obstructer, one must sleep to give the mind rest. Then specifically, during sleep, the tzadik sorts even more from the Chambers of Exchange, his soul ascends — the mind rising to where it rises, perceiving then what it perceives. This is the aspect of what is explained above (ois kaf-daled) in Parshas Vayaitzai : "he encountered the place... he lodged there... he dreamt" etc.; see there. Therefore one must take care to fall asleep amidst words of Torah, in order to sleep amidst joy — so that one does not taste the taste of death. This is David's plea: "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death." And it was established for every person to say before sleep in Birchas HaMapil : "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death" — as above. This is connected to: "how long shall I set counsel in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?" — followed by "look... illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death." He cried: since exile overpowers so greatly — its essence being sorrow and sadness ( "sorrow in my heart by day" ) — I plead: "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death" — that Hashem illuminate his eyes so he can gladden his soul, so his sleep will not be in the aspect of the side of death (= sorrow and sadness). The four times "how long" David cried in this mizmor correspond to the four exiles, as Rashi explains. The essence of all exiles is sadness. David cried and prayed that Israel be saved from sorrow and sadness — that their enemies not be exalted over them through this, chas v'shalom , that they not sleep the death. Therefore immediately follows: "but I trusted in Your kindness; my heart shall exult in Your salvation; I shall sing to Hashem" etc. He strengthened himself and all the souls of Israel encompassed in him: he trusts in His kindness, and through this gladdens himself — "my heart shall exult in Your salvation." This is the essential tikun for every person: to strengthen his heart in great trust in Hashem's kindnesses — certainly He will not abandon him — until he rejoices and exults: "my heart shall exult in Your salvation." But those who do not merit this — their sleep is seized by the side of death according to their flaw in the mind, and their dreams are confused, etc. (holy Zohar). Every flaw of the mind and da'as is due to the flaw of the Arranger and Settler — one does not merit the power of the Arranger and Settler of the mind as needed. If one had proper yishuv hada'as [settled mind], certainly he would not pursue follies and unbecoming actions. As explained elsewhere ( LM I:10 ): the essential distancing from Hashem is due to lacking yishuv hada'as . And: the essential yishuv hada'as is through joy, etc.; see there. One depends on the other: because one does not overpower with joy — at least being grateful for being saved, for not being made a gentile, for being separated from those who err in many asp

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part5
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 5 (§§ 51–61 / Oaseyos נא–סא) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 51 — "Yaakov Lived in Egypt Seventeen Years": True Life Through Transforming Sorrow to Joy "Yaakov lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years." It is explained in our Sages' words (Midrash Rabbah) and especially in the holy Zohar on this parshah that those seventeen years were the essential years of his life — he lived in joy and contentment, as stated there in the holy Zohar. At first glance this is astonishing: when he dwelt in Eretz Yisrael he had no peace, yet in impure Egypt — where the Egyptian exile began and they embittered their lives — specifically there he dwelt in peace! But all this is the aspect of "gladness and joy shall they attain" etc. The essential completeness of joy in Him (= the essential vitality) is when one overpowers to seize sorrow and sighing and transform it to joy — the essential sorting from the Chambers of Exchange, accomplished through joy, essentially through exchanging and transforming sorrow and sighing to joy. The totality of all the forefathers' service was to reveal and make known His G-dliness in the world — the sole purpose of man's existence, and all his joy and vitality. For it is known to all that this world is full of anger, anguish, sorrow, and sighing, ending in death, and the days of our lives are vanity, etc. There is no joy or vitality in the world except through the sparkling of truth and emunah . "Truth is the elixir of life," as our Sages say. The essential truth is Hashem: "the truth of Hashem is forever." To believe in the truth of His existence and to strive and labor all one's days to draw close and cling to Him: "to Him you shall cling" — this is all vitality: "choose life, so that you and your seed may live — to love Hashem your G-d and to cling to Him, for He is your life." But this clinging in completeness is impossible unless one shatters all bodily desires completely — like the forefathers, who merited drawing holy emunah upon themselves each time until they came to great joy through this. Through this they sorted each time from the Chambers of Exchange, ascending through all the above ascents, perceiving the Ain Sof light in mati v'lo mati — each according to his level, for there are many levels in this. The entire order of every Jew's daily service — especially the order of tefilah with tallis and tefillin , etc. — is all the aspect of the above ascents explained in the Torah " Amtza'isa ": raising Malchus from the klipos , Netzach-Hod-Yesod clothing Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes , and Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes clothing Chochmah-Binah-Da'as , etc. — from world to world; see the kavanos and the above Torah well, and a little will sparkle for you. Although the forefathers and great tzadikim shattered the body completely, meriting the essential completeness of this joy in Him ( "rejoice, tzadikim , in Hashem" ; "the righteous shall rejoice and exult before G-d and be glad with joy" ) — their entire labor was to rectify all the world, to draw this holy joy and vitality into the heart of every Jew. Even one who has not completely shattered his bodily desires can also draw close to Hashem through guarding the Torah and mitzvos . Even one who has flawed as he has flawed — whenever he desires and strives to draw close to Hashem, he can gladden and revive his soul through the great power of the tzadikim : by believing that every single good point merited through every mitzvah he performs is beyond measure. Even the good points of the mitzvos performed by the sinners of Israel surpass all the pleasures, wealth, etc. of the entire world — until they greatly gladden their souls that they too merit such true, eternal good: engaging in mitzvos , through which they cling to Hashem, the Life of all lives, the Source of the joy of all joys. As it says: "I shall come to the G-d of my joyful exultation" ; "You shall make known to me the path of life; fullness of joys is Your countenance" — all the aspect of "gladness and joy shall they attain" : seizing sorrow and sighing and transforming it to joy. This is the aspect of all the exiles Israel undergoes — whose essence is the exile of the soul, far from its Father in Heaven, whose essential exile is sadness, as above. Due to the sin of Adam HaRishon and the corruptions of each generation, one must be in exile — until, through the power of the great tzadikim , the sorting from the Chambers of Exchange is accomplished specifically through this. The essential sorting is through joy — transforming sorrow and sighing to joy. This is the aspect of Yosef's sale to Egypt, through which specifically they could survive in Egypt: "G-d sent me before you for sustenance." Yosef is the inflaming of joy through the above aspect, as above. Even Yaakov our father and his holy sons — the totalit

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaHodaah 6 Part6
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hahodaah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaHodaah [The Blessing of Thanksgiving] — Halachah 6 Part 6 (§§ 62–75 / Oaseyos סב–עה) COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 ( Amtza'isa D'Alma ) § 62 — SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive]: Time Derives from the Obstructer; Joy Gives Life to Time SheHechiyanu v'kiy'manu v'higi'anu laz'man hazeh [Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time] — blessed over every joy that comes from time to time. The essential Birchas SheHechiyanu [the Blessing of Who Has Kept Us Alive] is on the Yamim Tovim . The essential formation of time derives at its root from the aspect of the waiting until it settles, as above. In truth there is no time at all (as explained on "I have this day begotten you," LM II:61 ). All of time exists only for the sake of free will — man must pass through this world for the span of his allotted days in order to bind time to that which is above time. This world is in place and time; man must pass through it to bind the aspects of time and place to that which is above time (see Hilchos Milah 4 on the above Torah ). The essential time derives from the above waiting — the Arranger and Settler of the mind (= the obstructer). The essential tikun is through the joy of the mitzvah , through mi yaimar . Man comes to this world only for this: to know Hashem through the perception of the above nine chambers, through which the Ain Sof light is perceived in mati v'lo mati . All this is impossible except through the Arranger and Settler — the aspect of waiting until it settles. All the days of man's life are only in the aspect of waiting — so he may settle properly in true yishuv hada'as , through which he will perceive what he perceives according to his true service — what even the angels do not merit perceiving. For the angels cannot perceive His Ain Sof light in this manner like man can, because they did not properly rectify the Arranger and Settler — which is only rectified through the power of free will that only man possesses (see Hilchos Nefilas Apayim on the Torah " Amtza'isa "). They burn and clamor to perceive Him, and though their perception is very lofty, it has no comparison to the perception of the righteous man who was in this world and withstood his trials through free will — thereby meriting rectifying the mind. The essential tikun is rectifying the Arranger and Settler (= the waiting), from which all time derives. All of man's time — all the days of his life — are the aspect of waiting: he is told to wait the time of his life, to settle himself each day and each moment. Through this he will merit perceiving at each moment what he perceives, until on his final day he ascends with all the days and time he spent in this world — ascending to where he ascends, perceiving the lights of the tzachtzachos that the tzadikim merit: "He shall satisfy your soul with tzachtzachos " — fortunate are they. The essential thing is merited through performing mitzvos with joy. Joy is the vitality and sustenance of all man's days — for in truth there is no time at all. As we see even physically: they are nothing, for time flies exceedingly — a passing shadow, drifting dust, a fading cloud, etc. The past is gone, the future not yet here, and the present is but an eye-blink (as brought in many sefarim ). "The days of our lives are vanity, vanity of vanities" (Midrash Koheles, Parshah 1) — like the vapor of the seventh vessel, having no substance. Nothing remains of all past, present, and future time except what one snatches from it: some good — Torah, tefilah , tzedakah , good deeds, intense desire and longing for Hashem, closeness to tzadikim and true friends, etc. The essential thing is joy — the point of all mitzvos , the essential vitality and sustenance. Therefore the essential vitality (in time and place) is through the day and time one merits the joy of the mitzvah — rejoicing in Him: "this is the day Hashem has made — let us exult and rejoice in it." Only "this is the day Hashem has made" — when one merits exulting and rejoicing in it. From there comes all vitality and sustenance of the days and times (= the days of man's life). The wicked, who do not merit the joy of the mitzvah , truly have no vitality — therefore our Sages say: "the wicked in their lifetimes are called dead," since they do not merit binding time to that which is above time, receiving vitality from the Source of Life through the joy of the mitzvah . Conversely, even the great tzadikim , if they do not take care to wait until they settle properly and their minds pursue excessively — they cannot live in this world at all: "when they drew near before Hashem and died" ; "he peeked and died." Therefore the essential vitality of the days and times man lives in this world is through the above — meriting the tikun of the Settler and Arranger properly through performing mitzvos with joy. Then he merits coming and ascending with

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaMazon 4 Part1 (2)
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hamazon Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaMazon U'Mayim Acharonim — Halachah 4 Part 1 of 3 (§§ 1–9) COMPLETE FULL TRANSLATION Based on LM II:40 — "Mi She'yodai'a Mai'Eretz Yisrael" Whoever knows of Eretz Yisrael; his'pa'arus; the cup of blessing; Chanukah Halachic framework : Based on the Torah "Whoever knows of Eretz Yisrael ," etc. ( Likutay Tinyana, Siman 40 ) — see there, the entire Torah well. § 1 — The Holiness of Eretz Yisrael Through His'pa'arus The general principle: The essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael is through "the eyes of Hashem" — through Hashem constantly gazing there — through which "the air of Eretz Yisrael makes wise," for eyes are associated with chochmah [wisdom]. The essential aspect of "the eyes of Hashem" is aroused through the his'pa'arus [glorification] that Hashem takes in Israel, in the aspect of "Yisrael, in whom I take pride [ espa'ir ]." This is the aspect of tefillin , etc. Whoever gazes upon this his'pa'arus — in him too there are formed the aspect of mochin of tefillin , and the mochin break through into the eyes. Then wherever he gazes, the air becomes the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , as above. However, the his'pa'arus of Hashem Himself — not everyone merits to see. But one who gazes upon the tzadik , and especially at the time when the world gathers to him — i.e. on Rosh HaShanah , when the essential gathering takes place — then much his'pa'arus ascends from the aforementioned gathering of those who come together for the sake of serving Hashem. And the tzadik is comprised of all this his'pa'arus , for the essential his'pa'arus that Hashem takes in Israel is through the tzadik who draws them close to Hashem — through which Hashem takes pride in them. It emerges that the tzadik himself is the essential his'pa'arus . Therefore whoever gazes with his eyes upon the tzadik draws upon himself also from this his'pa'arus — the aspect of tefillin — and then the his'pa'arus and mochin break through into the eyes. Then wherever this person gazes, Eretz Yisrael is formed as well, for the essential [holiness of] Eretz Yisrael is formed through the eyes drawn through the his'pa'arus , etc., as above — see all this there well. § 2 — The Cup of Birchas HaMazon : Gazing at His'pa'arus This is the aspect of: the cup of Birchas HaMazon — one must place one's eyes upon it. For the essence of Birchas HaMazon is to reveal the holiness of Eretz Yisrael , from which the essential holiness and tikkun of eating [derives], as explained elsewhere (above in Hilchos Devarim HaNohagin BiS'udah — see there). As it is written: "and you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless Hashem your G-d for the good land that He gave you." The essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael is revealed through the eyes — through gazing upon the his'pa'arus of Israel, as above. This is the aspect of the cup of Birchas HaMazon after the eating of Israel. For the cup of blessing is the aspect of the totality of the his'pa'arus — that which Hashem takes pride in Israel — through which great joy and delight are made in all the worlds. For conversely, chas v'shalom , when one of Israel falls from his avodah , chas v'shalom — the aspect of "and He was grieved in His heart." As our Sages zichronam livrachah said: "What does the Shechinah say? 'My head is heavy upon Me, My arm is heavy upon Me.'" As this teaching is brought in the aforementioned Torah . But conversely — when Israel draws close to Hashem and He takes pride in them — then strength and delight are added in all the worlds, in the aspect of "Hashem rejoices in His works," the aspect of "the work of My hands in which to take pride." Hashem rejoices and is glad, kivyachol , in the greatness of the his'pa'arus He receives from Israel — for this is the essence of His delight and joy. As it is written regarding our his'pa'arus — that we take pride in Him: "in Your Name they rejoice all day... for You are the glory of their strength." For his'pa'arus is joy. As it is written: "He will beautify the humble with salvation; the devout will exult in glory." And it is written: "I will rejoice greatly in Hashem, my soul will exult in my G-d, for He has clothed me in garments of salvation, a robe of righteousness He has wrapped me, like a groom who adorns himself with pe'er," etc. It emerges that his'pa'arus is joy. This is the aspect of wine that gladdens — which is the wine of the cup of blessing, as it is written: "wine gladdens the heart of man." That is: the wine of holiness — the wine of blessing — is the aspect of joy, the aspect of the totality of the his'pa'arus , which is joy, as above. For "song is said only over wine," as our Sages zichronam livrachah said on the verse "that gladdens G-d and men" (Shoftim 9), etc. — from here [we learn that] song is said only over wine. And all the songs and praises are the aspect of his'pa'arus — that we praise and glorify Him with song and joy and praise and gladnes

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaMazon 4 Part2a
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hamazon Part a Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaMazon U'Mayim Acharonim — Halachah 4 Part 2a (§§ 10–12) COMPLETE FULL TRANSLATION · Based on LM II:40 § 10 — Parshas HaNesi'im on Chanukah: the Colors of His'pa'arus Therefore we read Parshas HaNesi'im on Chanukah. For the nesi'im of Israel are the aspect of the tzadikai hador , in whom the essential his'pa'arus is comprised, as explained in the aforementioned Torah . Therefore the nesi'im brought the filling-stones for the aifod and the choshen . For the stones of the aifod and choshen are the aspect of the revelation of the his'pa'arus that Hashem takes in Israel. For the essential his'pa'arus is through the gvanin [colors] — through Israel being composed of gavanin sagin [many colors], as explained in the words of Rabbainu zichrono livrachah elsewhere. The totality of the colors of Israel were revealed in the stones of the choshen and aifod , where each stone had its own unique color according to its tribe whose name was inscribed upon it — i.e. according to the color and his'pa'arus that Hashem receives from that tribe. For each tribe has its own unique color. All these colors were in the stones of the choshen and aifod — odem for Reuvain, pitdah for Shimon, etc. These colors were depicted on the degalim [banners], as our Sages zichronam livrachah said. With these banners Israel went to milchemes mitzvah to conquer Eretz Yisrael — this was the essential war of Israel. For the essential conquest of Eretz Yisrael is through the revelation of the his'pa'arus , which is the totality of the colors of the choshen stones depicted on the banners. Through this the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is formed and its taste revealed — and then all obstacles to Eretz Yisrael are subdued. For the essential obstacles are those who bring an evil report about the land, etc., as Rabbainu zichrono livrachah writes in the Torah "Tisha Tikkunin" — see there. Therefore specifically the nesi'im brought the stones of the choshen and aifod . For the essential his'pa'arus depends on the nesi'im , who are the tzadikai hador , through whom the essential his'pa'arus [comes], as above. Therefore we read Parshas HaNesi'im on Chanukah, for then we reveal the light of this his'pa'arus , whose essence depends on the tzadikai hador , who are the aspect of nesi'im , as above. § 11 — Three Levels of Ner Chanukah : Three Gazings This is the aspect of the mitzvah of ner Chanukah : ner ish u'vaiso [one candle per household]; the mehadrin — one candle for each person; and the mehadrin min hamehadrin — adding and increasing. For in ner Chanukah there are mehadrin and mehadrin min hamehadrin . For the essence of ner Chanukah is in the aspect of hidur and his'pa'arus — that we reveal the his'pa'arus of Hashem, that He takes pride and beautifies Himself in us, as above. This is the aspect of the three levels in the mitzvah of ner Chanukah — corresponding to the three aspects of drawing the holiness of Eretz Yisrael explained in the aforementioned Torah . For it is explained there that through the his'pa'arus Hashem takes in Israel, the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is formed through the gazing of the eyes of Hashem there. Also, whoever merits to gaze upon this his'pa'arus through gazing at the tzadik — he draws upon himself the aspect of "the eyes of Hashem," and wherever he gazes, avira d'Eretz Yisrael is formed. But who can merit to see the his'pa'arus of Hashem? Only one who merits to see the true tzadik , who is the essential his'pa'arus of Israel. Then he too merits to receive from this his'pa'arus , and the aspect of the aforementioned eyes are formed in him, and wherever he gazes, Eretz Yisrael is formed — as explained there, see there well. It emerges that there are three aspects of the gazing of the eyes through which the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is formed: (1) the gazing of the light of the eyes of Hashem; (2) the gazing of the tzadik , who is the totality of the his'pa'arus ; (3) the gazing of the eyes of each person who merits to see the tzadik . The essential one is the tzadik , for he is comprised of all the his'pa'arus of Israel — all are drawn close to Hashem through him. Also, the tzadik can see the his'pa'arus of Hashem Himself. For even though Rabbainu writes there: "Who can see the his'pa'arus of Hashem?" — this was said regarding ordinary people, who certainly do not merit to see Hashem and His his'pa'arus . But the true tzadikim see Hashem and His his'pa'arus , as we find with the prophets. As it is written: "and I saw Hashem" (Yeshayah 6). And Michayahu said: "I saw Hashem sitting," etc. (Melachim I, 22). Therefore the tzadikim themselves certainly see the his'pa'arus of Hashem Himself. And they themselves are the essential his'pa'arus , as above. Therefore the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael is revealed through the tzadik , who is the totality of all the his'pa'arus , through which the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is for

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaMazon 4 Part2b
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hamazon Part b Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaMazon U'Mayim Acharonim — Halachah 4 Part 2b (§§ 13–16) COMPLETE FULL TRANSLATION · Based on LM II:40 § 13 — " Your Stature Resembles a Palm Tree " This is the aspect of Hashem praising Israel: "your stature resembles a palm tree" — meaning that they are strong and hard and firm in their avodah and do not allow themselves to be felled in any way. As Rashi explains there regarding the image of Nevuchadnetzar: they stood in their uprightness and did not bow down to it. For this is the praise and his'pa'arus of Israel, as above. § 14 — " Komemiyus " — Upright Stature Toward Eretz Yisrael This is the aspect of: "and I led you komemiyus [upright]" — and Rashi explains: with upright stature. For this verse was said regarding Eretz Yisrael , where Israel was heading. For all the journeys and paths and travels of Israel, and all the wars and conquests — all were to go and conquer Eretz Yisrael , as is understood and explained in the narratives of the entire Torah. This is: "and I led you komemiyus" — with upright stature — the aspect of azus and stubbornness, standing upright with great stubbornness to win the war and go and come to Eretz Yisrael , which was the essential purpose of the Exodus, etc., as above. For it is impossible to come to Eretz Yisrael — to win this war which is the essential totality of all the wars of the Jewish person — except through very great stubbornness, the aspect of "and I led you komemiyus." The aspect of [what we say in prayer]: "and lead us speedily komemiyus to our land — speedily in our days, Amain." § 15 — Eight Days of Chanukah = Eight Garments of the Kohain Gadol Therefore the miracle was through the kohanim , who wear garments of his'pa'arus , as it is written: "and you shall make holy garments for Aharon your brother, for kavod and for tiferes." The essential one is the Kohain Gadol , who wore the choshen and aifod upon which were inscribed the names of the children of Israel. There all the colors shone — the aspect of odem , pitdah , and barekes , etc. — each stone having its own unique color — which are the totality of the his'pa'arus of Israel, as above. Therefore there are eight days of Chanukah, corresponding to the eight garments of the Kehunah Gedolah [High Priesthood], which are the totality of the his'pa'arus — from which the essential light of ner Chanukah [derives], as above. Therefore Parshas Bigdai Kehunah is adjacent to the parshah of "and they shall take for you olive oil," etc. — which is the aspect of ner Chanukah , as above. This is: "and they established these eight days of Chanukah to give thanks and praise to Your great Name." For the hoda'os [thanks] and hallel [praise] are the his'pa'arus — that we praise and extol and glorify Him — through which Hashem is glorified and magnified and sanctified in all the worlds. This is the essential holiness of Chanukah, as above. § 16 — Parshas Vayehi Mikaitz on Chanukah: Breaking the Desire for Money Therefore we read Parshas Vayehi Mikaitz on Chanukah. For it is stated at the end of the aforementioned Torah that speaks of Eretz Yisrael , etc. — and it concludes there: "And there are still more matters in this — for 'a person does not die with half his desire in his hand.' It emerges that one's desire and will for money is never fulfilled, for one is always lacking, as above. But there is an aspect of doubled abundance — the aspect of 'and abundant silver to you,' which is a doubled expression. It emerges that with this abundance, one's desire is fulfilled, since it is doubled." And [Rabbainu] did not conclude further — end quote. Now, Rabbainu zichrono livrachah did not explain his words — what connection this matter has with everything he said previously regarding Eretz Yisrael and Rosh HaShanah , etc. But what appears to my humble understanding, I will explain somewhat: The desire for money — i.e. the fact that "a person does not die with half his desire in his hand," and the more he has, the more he lacks — this is the aspect of the blemish of the eyes, in the aspect of "and also his eye is not satisfied with wealth" (Koheles 4). And the blemish of the eyes is the aspect of the blemish of Eretz Yisrael . For the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael is drawn from the eyes — that gaze upon the tzadik who is comprised of all the his'pa'arus — through which the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is drawn. Eretz Yisrael is the source of blessing, for all blessings and abundances are drawn from Eretz Yisrael , as is known. For Eretz Yisrael receives its holiness from the tzadik , as above. And by the tzadik are all the blessings and abundances, in the aspect of "blessings upon the head of the tzadik," the aspect of "the tzadik is gracious and gives." When one merits to receive the abundance of Eretz Yisrael and the tzadik in completeness, certainly one has no lack at all. For regarding Eretz Yisrael it is written:

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Birchas HaMazon 4 Part3a
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Birchas Hamazon Part a Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Birchas HaMazon U'Mayim Acharonim — Halachah 4 Part 3a (§§ 17–19) COMPLETE · Based on LM II:40 § 17 — Pharaoh's Dream: Seven Cows and the Desire for Money This is the aspect of Pharaoh's dream — seven good cows and seven bad cows, the aspect of seven years of plenty and seven years of famine. This is the desire for money — the more one has, the more one lacks. Seven healthy good cows — the seven years of plenty — wealth and all good that Hashem gives the wealthy. "And behold seven other cows came up after them... and the lean bad cows swallowed the beautiful healthy cows." The seven bad cows are the seven years of famine — the desire for money, always hungry to swallow much wealth. They swallow the seven years of plenty — all the good Hashem gave him. The more wealth he has, the more he lacks — "one who increases possessions increases worry." He has worries as though actually poor — "they came into their belly and it was not known... their appearance was as bad as at first." Through the evil of the desire for money — the seven years of famine — all abundance is swallowed and forgotten, the wealth unknown to him. He is full of worry as before, always lacking — never having half his desire, "his eye never satisfied with wealth." His ever-growing desire swallows all his wealth until all good is unknown, swallowed through the constantly growing desire. The tikkun is through Yosef — the tzadik of the generation — through whom the essential tikkun of the desire for money comes. He counsels the wealthy to be saved from the seven years of famine — from the hunger of the desire for money — through tzedakah , the essential breaking of the desire for money, as Rabbainu writes ( Siman 13 ). This is "let Pharaoh act and appoint officers" — the aspect of gaba'ai tzedakah , officials looking after the poor. "And he shall take a fifth [v'chimaish]" — tzedakah whose measure is a fifth: "one who is generous should not give more than a fifth." "And the food shall be as a deposit for the land" — the essential safeguarding of wealth is through tzedakah : "my fathers stored below, I stored above." "The salt of money is its diminishment" (Kesubos 66). "And the land shall not be cut off by famine" — the hunger of money-desire should not cut off and uproot a person, as explained in "Tzavis Tzedek" ( Siman 23 ). Through tzedakah , one is saved. "He placed food in the cities... the food of the field of the city around it he placed within it" — he gave the food to the poor of that city, for "the poor of your city take precedence." As Rashi explains: each land preserves its produce by putting soil from the land into it. The poor person is the aspect of "dust" — "He raises the poor from the dust." To preserve wealth from the seven years of famine, one must put "soil of the land" — the merit of tzedakah given to the poor, the aspect of dust — into one's wealth. This preserves it from the desire for money that consumes life and wealth chas v'shalom . Yosef said to his brothers: "you are meraglim; to see the nakedness of the land you have come." He hinted at the blemish of the meraglim who blemished Eretz Yisrael .
