teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Krias Shma Sheal HaMitah H1-H2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Krias Shma Sheal Hamitah H H Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Krias Shma She'al HaMitah [Laws of the Bedtime Shma ] Halachos 1–2 Halachah 1 Based on LM I:36 ( "Bikrov Alai M'rayim" ) — see there the entire Torah. The general principle: every soul of Israel is rooted in the seventy souls of the House of Yaakov. And they are rooted in the seventy facets of Torah etc. And "corresponding to this" etc. are the seventy languages etc. And know that the desire for licentiousness is the generality of the evil traits of the seventy languages etc. And for this reason our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "and you shall not go astray... and after your eyes" — this refers to the desire for licentiousness etc., because it is the generality of the evil traits of the seventy languages etc. And know that the tikun for licentious thoughts that come upon a person is to say "Shma" and "Baruch Shaim" etc. For the desire for licentiousness comes from the turbidity of the blood etc. — which is Malchus of the Sitra Achra . And Malchusa d'Shamaya [the Sovereignty of Heaven] is in the aspect of "the mistress" — the G-d-fearing woman — which is in the aspect of the Sea of Shlomo standing upon twelve oxen, the twelve tribes of Y-ah. And when a person accepts upon himself the sovereignty of Heaven through these verses — including his soul among the twelve tribes of Y-ah and separating his soul from the souls of the Airev Rav [Mixed Multitude] who derive from the harlot etc., which is the evil maidservant — then it is in the aspect of "I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai" etc.: the desire flees and separates from him etc. For in these two verses — "Shma" and "Baruch Shaim" — there are twelve words, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Y-ah. And forty-nine letters, corresponding to the forty-nine letters in the names of the tribes of Y-ah etc. And through the acceptance of the sovereignty of Heaven etc., one's soul is included among the souls of the tribes of Y-ah — the aspect of the G-d-fearing woman. Then it is the aspect of closing the eyes during Krias Shma , to indicate that through the acceptance of the sovereignty of Heaven, the "beautiful maiden who has no eyes" — which is the desire that encompasses the evil traits of the seventy languages etc. — [is subdued]. And when the revelation of Torah comes, new souls are made from the revelation etc., each according to his aspect and grasp. For the Torah has two powers etc. And this is a great principle: from the Mouth of the Most High nothing goes forth but simple light, but according to the aspect of the vessel that receives the light, so the light is imaged within it etc. And this is the aspect of: "behold, I have received [the command] to bless, and He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it" etc. And the essential tikun and perfection of the vessel is through guarding the Bris [holy covenant]. And then one merits to receive the light and to image it in the aspect of blessing etc. — see there all of this well. It emerges that through Krias Shma , licentious thoughts are subdued. For through Krias Shma one is included in Malchus d'K'dushah , among the twelve tribes of Y-ah etc. And this is the aspect of Krias Shma She'al HaMitah . For the essential tikun of sleep is to be saved from evil thoughts. As we pray and beseech from Hashem in the berachah of HaMapil before sleep: "and may my thoughts and evil dreams and evil contemplations not frighten me" etc. For it is known that the essential intensification of the flaw mentioned above — the flaw of the desire for licentiousness — is in the aspect of sleep, in the aspect of mikrei lailah [nocturnal occurrences], G-d forbid. Therefore before sleep one must subdue these thoughts mentioned above. And for this reason our Sages of blessed memory ordained for us to recite Krias Shma She'al HaMitah before sleep — which is a very great tikun for the flaw of the desire mentioned above, as explained in the Writings [of the Ari"zal]. For through reciting Krias Shma and accepting upon oneself the sovereignty of Heaven, through this one separates his soul from the souls of the Airev Rav etc. as mentioned above, and includes his soul among the twelve tribes of Y-ah etc. — which is the aspect of the G-d-fearing woman, the aspect of Malchus d'K'dushah , the aspect of the mistress. Through this, the thoughts that derive from the harlot are subdued and flee from him, as mentioned above, in the aspect of "I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai." As explained well in the Torah mentioned above — see there. And this is the aspect of what we say: "and may my bed be complete before You" etc. A complete bed — this is the aspect of the bed of Yaakov, of the twelve tribes of Y-ah, which was a complete bed. As our Sages of blessed memory said on the verse "and Yisra'el bowed upon the head of the bed" : that his bed was complete — twelve tribes of Y-ah without any refuse etc. And this is wha

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos netilas yadayim liseuda  Betzias HaPas Part1 10-21
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Netilas Yadayim Liseuda Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 1: §§ 10–21) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — continuation of Halacha 6. § 10 — The Laws of Betzi'as HaPas And this is the aspect of betzi'as hapas [breaking the bread], in which there are many laws concerning the breaking. Our Sages investigated and expounded and debated at length regarding the breaking, as is written in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 102) : "From where do you begin HaMotzi ?" etc. — from which it is understood that there are deep secrets in this (as was already explained in the preceding halachos ). For the entire tikkun of betzi'as hapas that our Sages were so precise about — is that one needs to break the bread with the berachah in such a manner that he merits at the time of eating the illumination of Ratzon explained in the Torah teaching. For it is explained there that through the inclusiveness of the son and student, one merits at the time of eating the wondrous illumination of Ratzon . For the Malchus — the aspect of yirah — receives sustenance from the hands in yam hachochmah , which are the remazim ; there the makifin [surrounding lights] shine, which are the aspect of mah , the aspect of silence. And this is the aspect of "one does not converse during a meal" — see there well. § 11 — The Ten Fingers on the Bread And this is the aspect of what is written in the Shulchan Aruch : that one must place his ten fingers upon the bread at the time of breaking — to indicate that the bread one eats is drawn from the hands in yam hachochmah mentioned above. Through this, the holiness of eating — whose essence is to merit the illumination of Ratzon drawn through the hands, which are the remazim , as above. § 12 — Break from Where the Fire Struck Most And this is the aspect of: "From where do you begin HaMotzi ? From the place that crusted ( d'karim b'shulah )." For the eating of Israel must be in great holiness. And the primary food that satisfies a person is the bread . Therefore it has ten mitzvos , as written in the Tur and Shulchan Aruch , for one must refine the grain and the bread through many stages of refinement. This is the aspect of all the labors and exertions invested in grain until it becomes bread: plowing, sowing, reaping, separating from chaff and straw, then grinding, sifting, and cleaning from bran and husks, etc. All of this derives from the sin of Adam HaRishon, whose sin was in eating — he ate from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, and then it was decreed upon him: "By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread" (Genesis 3:19) — which is all the labors mentioned above until it becomes bread. And all of this is for the sake of refining — to eliminate the bad and the waste and to refine the good. Therefore, the essential spiritual refinement is accomplished by Israel through the ten mitzvos pertaining to bread. And all these refinements — refining the good from the bad, the food from the waste, cleaning the grain from chaff and straw (which are the klipos that precede the fruit) — are all to refine the holy emunah that Adam HaRishon blemished. This is accomplished by driving away and eliminating from the mind the kushyos [difficulties/questions] in every person's heart, from which all forms of heresy derive — which are the klipos , the chaff and straw covering the wheat. As is understood from the Tikunai Zohar and the Holy Zohar regarding the refinement of the halachah — which is the aspect of refining the wheat from the chaff and straw — for it is all one matter. For through eating, vitality is drawn to a person. And the essential vitality is da'as and chochmah , as it is written: "Wisdom gives life" (Ecclesiastes 7:12) . Therefore food at its root — especially bread, which is the main thing — is very exalted, for rooted within it is power and vitality that is the aspect of chochmah to give life to a person and bind his soul to his body. But since the sin of Adam HaRishon, much waste surrounds the bread — chaff and straw, etc. — which are the kushyos , the confusion of da'as that surround the mind until one cannot understand the halachah properly. These are the laws of the holy Torah, and for this one must labor greatly to refine the halachah from the kushyos — the chaff and straw — as is found in the Tikunai Zohar . And even more, one must refine the bread from the kushyos and waste that seek to confuse holy emunah — for this is the main thing. For the primary rectification of eating is through emunah , as explained elsewhere ( LM I, 62 ). For the primary sustaining and completeness of da'as is through emunah , as Rabbainu explains many times. And this itself is the illumination of Ratzon , the aspect of silence mentioned above, that one merits during eating — each according to what he merits to receive from his true Rebbe , the illumination of son and student. For the illuminatio

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos netilas yadayim liseuda  Betzias HaPas Part5 57-68
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Netilas Yadayim Liseuda Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 5: §§ 57–68) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — continuation. § 57 — "Who Is Rich?" — Happy with His Portion Next: "Who is rich? He who is happy with his portion." For it is already explained in the Torah teaching that through the da'as — the inclusiveness of son and student = conquering the yetzer , illuminating da'as to drive away the ruach shtus from which all sins derive — one merits to receive sustenance and wealth from yam hachochmah , from the hands that are the remazim — the illumination of Ratzon . The essential sustenance and wealth is drawn from yam hachochmah through bitachon , as explained there on the verse: "all look to You expectantly" (Psalms 104:27) . Through this, sustenance is received, where Ratzon shines — "and satisfies every living being with Ratzon ." Then sustenance is ground and divided to each as appropriate — as explained on the verse about Livyasan ( "whom You formed to sport in it" ). "Who is rich? He who is happy with his portion" — for the true wealth is when one merits to receive wealth in holiness from yam hachochmah , from the hands there. Then one receives the illumination of Ratzon and is certainly happy with his portion — the aspect of Ratzon , "satisfying every living being with Ratzon " — accepting with Ratzon whatever Hashem bestows upon him, since such is His will. The proof-text: "The labor of your hands, when you eat [of it]" (Psalms 128:2) — "your hands" specifically: one receives eating and sustenance from the palms and hands in yam hachochmah , through bitachon , lifting one's eyes to heaven, stretching out one's palms to Him: "I spread out my hands to You." Then certainly: "fortunate are you in this world, and it is good for you in the World to Come." For the essential delight of the World to Come is the wondrous illumination of Ratzon — "how great is Your goodness that You have stored for those who fear You." And one who merits the illumination of Ratzon even in this world — fortunate is he even here, for the Ratzon that shines upon him is a taste of the World to Come. § 58 — "Who Is Honored?" — Honoring the Creatures "Who is honored? He who honors the creatures." As it says: "those who honor Me, I will honor; those who scorn Me shall be degraded" (I Samuel 2:30) . This seems puzzling: how does this verse — which speaks only of honoring Hashem — prove that the honored one is he who honors creatures ? But according to all the above, it is well understood. The Tanna concludes with what he began. He started with "Who is wise?" — the wisdom and da'as to recognize Hashem, which is the essential wisdom: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom… but in this let him glory — understanding and knowing Me" (Jeremiah 9:22-23) . And the essential wisdom is to know and believe that "the whole earth is full of His glory" — Hashem chooses the service of the lower ones in this world, and in them His glory is primarily revealed. Therefore one must certainly honor the creatures , for through this one honors Hashem. One must believe that in every member of Israel, His glory is clothed. From every Jew — even the worst of the worst — as long as he is within the holy emunah , Hashem receives particular honor and pride. "Over Israel is His pride and His glory." Therefore one must honor every person. The essential honor is to speak with each person about the ultimate purpose — instilling yiras Shamayim in him, and receiving from him as well — "receiving from one another" — the aspect of "learning from every person" with which he began. For this is the essential honor — "there is no honor but Torah." As Rabbainu instructed in the Torah teaching: every person must engage in this — instilling da'as in his fellow. This is the essential honor of Hashem. Therefore the proof-text: "those who honor Me, I will honor" — for this is the essential honor of Hashem. § 59 — The Sons of Eli: The Opposite of Aharon The verse "those who honor Me, I will honor" was said regarding the sons of Eli, who scorned Israel and the sacrifices. They did the opposite of what they should have done as Kohanim — for the essential holiness of the Kohen is the inclusiveness of son and student. The Kohanim offer all the sacrifices through which the inclusiveness of upper and lower is accomplished. But the sons of Eli blemished this greatly — scorning Israel and the sacrifices. Therefore the prophet rebuked them: "Did I not reveal Myself to the house of your father in Egypt?" (I Samuel 2:27) — referring to Aharon, the first Kohen (as Rashi explains). Why don't you follow the path of your father Aharon, from whom all the holiness of the Kehunah derives? For Aharon engaged in drawing the da'as to Israel in ultimate completeness. He was "one who loves peace and pursues peace, loves the creatures and brings them close to the Tora

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos netilas yadayim liseuda  Betzias HaPas Part6 60-87 end
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Netilas Yadayim Liseuda Betzias Hapas Part End Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 6 — Final: §§ 69–87) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — conclusion. § 69 — Birchas HaMazon : Drawing Ratzon Through Speech This is the aspect of Birchas HaMazon . The essential tikkun of eating is to merit the illumination of Ratzon that will shine in the future — "You give them their food in its time" — "at the time, it shall be said to Yaakov and Yisrael: mah has G-d wrought!" — "how great is Your goodness that You have stored for those who fear You." Therefore the Torah commanded Birchas HaMazon after eating — so each Jew draws upon himself the illumination of Ratzon through the holy speech of blessing, thanking, and praising Hashem for his food. All blessings and thanksgivings to His great Name are the aspect of Ratzon , for Shemo [His Name] = Ratzon in gematria . All are included in the ten types of melody — blessing, thanksgiving, etc. — all aspects of wondrous devekus and intense yearning. Therefore the essential Birchas HaMazon is over the cup of wine — "song is only said over wine" — the aspect of devekus and Ratzon . § 70 — The Three Berachos of Birchas HaMazon The three berachos correspond to the three aspects of inclusiveness. The first berachah — instituted by Moshe when the man descended — the aspect of mah , the upper dwellers. Moshe's comprehension is mah — the lower included in the upper. The man : "They called its name man , for they did not know mah it was." The second berachah — Birchas Ha'aretz — instituted by Yehoshua: the illumination of the lower dwellers, "the whole earth is full of His glory." His glory is revealed primarily in Eretz Yisrael . Yehoshua is the student — his comprehension is Melo . The third berachah — Boneh Yerushalayim — instituted by Dovid and Shlomo when the Bais HaMikdash was built: inclusiveness of both = the essential union of the worlds. Through all three, the illumination of Ratzon during eating is drawn — " mah " specifically. § 71 — HaTov V'HaMeitiv : Burial of the Slain of Beitar The berachah of HaTov V'HaMeitiv — instituted at Yavneh for the slain of Beitar who were given burial. The essential true and eternal good is the illumination of Ratzon that each will merit in the future — "how great is Your goodness stored for those who fear You." In the future, all will bless HaTov V'HaMeitiv on everything — understanding that all that passes over a person serves his eternal good. After the destruction, the Sages added this fourth berachah — drawing Ratzon from the World to Come into this world. When the Bais HaMikdash stood, Ratzon flowed through the three berachos . Now: "a person's table atones" — a fourth berachah is needed. Burial is the tikkun of the dead — the sprouting of eternal life: "the dust returns to the earth, and the spirit returns to G-d" . The Midrash: "the day of death is better than the day of birth" — when alive, counted toward death; when dead, counted toward life. But only after burial, for the soul has no rest until then. The higher the soul ascends, the more it illuminates below. The body decomposes in the earth, eliminating the contamination from Adam's sin — whose blemish was through eating from the Tree of Knowledge, blemishing the illumination of Ratzon . When the Sages saw the slain of Beitar were not being permitted burial, they feared hope was lost. The slain of Beitar had brought the destruction closer by lighting candles on the anniversary of the Churban . But when Hashem had mercy through the tzadikim 's prayers and they were given burial — the Sages saw: "the kindnesses of Hashem have not ended." They instituted HaTov V'HaMeitiv specifically in Birchas HaMazon — because the illumination of Ratzon is drawn during eating. Now after the destruction, we must strengthen with ever stronger Ratzon — sustaining ourselves through yearning for the Bais HaMikdash , reciting the sacrifices: "our lips shall substitute for bulls." § 72 — Yirmiyahu's Lament and Self-Comfort Yirmiyahu lamented: "My endurance has perished, and my hope from Hashem" (Lamentations 3:18) . But he comforts himself: "This I take to heart, therefore I have hope: the kindnesses of Hashem have not ended, for His mercies are not consumed. They are new every morning ; great is Your faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:21-23) . "New every morning" = techiyas hameisim — all souls renewed, living eternal life = the illumination of Ratzon . Despite everything: "Hashem is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope for Him." Now in the depth of exile, each must strengthen in Ratzon — waiting with great yearning. The more Ratzon one draws upon himself amid exile, the more he merits the great good stored for the future. § 73 — Bein HaMetzarim : Mourning, Machlokes , and Mah vs. Lanu Bein HaMetzarim — mourning the destruction caused by the meraglim : "You wept for nothing; I will esta

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos netlias yadayim liseuda  Betzias HaPas Part4 44-56
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Netlias Yadayim Liseuda Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah — Betzi'as HaPas (Part 4: §§ 44–56) Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) — continuation. § 44 — Silence in the End of Days "Therefore the wise man at that time shall be silent" (Amos 5:13) . "To You, silence is praise, O G-d, in Tzion" (Psalms 65:2) . "Only to G-d be my soul silent" (Psalms 62:6) . "It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of Hashem" (Lamentations 3:26) . And many such verses. For now, in these end of days about which these verses were prophesied, one must be silent greatly about everything happening in the world — not to enter into investigations, kushyos , and terutzim at all — only to be silent and wait for the salvation of Hashem. Until, for the most part, through the silence, his heart will burn until he cries out and prays to Hashem, in the aspect of: "I was mute in silence, I was still… my heart grew hot within me; in my musing a fire burned; I spoke with my tongue" (Psalms 39:3-4) . And this is: "He enlarges nations and destroys them" (Job 12:23) — "He captures the wise in their own craftiness" (Job 5:13) . All of this was at Krias Yam Suf , where [Hashem] deliberately surrounded them to mislead [the Egyptians], as it is written: "Let them turn back and encamp before Pi HaChiros…" "And Pharaoh said…" And so it is now. And those who are pursued must be careful not to walk in cleverness — only to cry out to Hashem. And if even that is difficult, at the very least not to question [His ways], and certainly not to speak against His attributes — only to be silent and wait, "until He looks down and sees" (Lamentations 3:50) , and to await His kindness alone: "Hashem shall fight for you, and you shall be silent" . As it is written: "We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You" (II Chronicles 20:12) , and: "For we have no strength against this great multitude… help us, for we lean upon You" (II Chronicles 14:10) . Especially now, at the end of this exile, about which Yirmiyahu said: "Waters flowed over my head… I called Your Name, Hashem, from the lowest pit" (Lamentations 3:54-55) , and: "It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of Hashem" — "until He looks down and sees from heaven, for Hashem will not cast off forever" . For the essential persecution of the pursuers — whether from the nations or among Israel itself, where the disputants fiercely pursue the upright — is mainly through empty cleverness : everyone imagining himself wise and understanding, wanting everyone to follow his crooked path. And it seems to him that he must pursue the pursued. But the pursued must be especially careful not to be misled by their evil smooth words — only to look at the truth for truth's sake, and to fulfill: "Do not answer a fool according to his folly" (Proverbs 26:4) . Only to be silent, even in one's mind — not to enter into kushyos and terutzim — only to await the salvation of Hashem, in the aspect of what Moshe told Israel at Krias Yam Suf : "Fear not, stand firm and see the salvation of Hashem… Hashem shall fight for you, and you shall be silent." Only now, since a complete redemption is needed with no exile afterward, and the sitra achra and yetzer hara are spreading enormously, one must extend his patience even more and strengthen himself to be silent in his mind — not to question Hashem or the true yir'ei Hashem , but to strive to cry out and pray to Hashem greatly. As the Tanna repeated many times: "In the footsteps of Mashiach , insolence will increase… those who fear sin [will be despised]… truth will be absent" — and our Sages expounded that truth will be made into "flocks upon flocks," each one saying the truth is with him — until the conclusion each time: "Upon whom can we lean? Only upon our Father in heaven." This is repeated multiple times, and each time the confusion and accusation of these end of days is revealed, it concludes: upon whom can we lean if not upon our Father in heaven? — as explained in Sotah , see there. The essence: the main pursuit of the pursuers against the upright and the sincere is that they want to ensnare them with their evil cleverness and abundant mockery — and this is the hardest of all, for the main thing is the prevention of the mind . First they pursue them openly; then they try even harder to seduce them with smooth words, claiming they seek their good — and this is hardest of all. Therefore it is impossible to describe everything involved — only: the wise man at that time shall be silent and understand where the truth is, and fulfill the words of the Tannaim who repeated: upon whom can we lean if not upon our Father in heaven. § 45 — Purification of the Blood Through Eating Let us return to the matter of the counting. It is explained in the Kavanos that during the Sefirah we engage in rectifying and purifying the blood , the main thing being that the blood should

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos seuda 5  Betzias HaPas 5 Part1 1-13
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Seuda Betzias Hapas Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Betzi'as HaPas — Halachah 5 Part 1: §§ 1–13 Based on "L'Hamshich Shalom" ( LM I, 14 ) Halachic framework: One must bless HaMotzi on a whole loaf. The blessing must conclude together with the bread [i.e. one must hold the bread while completing the berachah ]. The Sages always called the one blessing HaMotzi the " botze'a " [breaker], not simply "the one who blesses." The Shulchan Aruch called these laws " Hilchos Betzi'as HaPas " — Laws of Breaking Bread. Similarly, all eating or giving bread to the poor is described in terms of breaking/splitting: "is it not to break your bread for the hungry?" The Sages deliberated at length from where on the loaf one should break it, concluding: from where the baking began ( mei'haicha d'kadim bishula ), or from where it completed. § 1 — The Whole Loaf: Yirah and Shalom The essential principle from LM I:14 : one must complete the yirah [fear/awe of Hashem] through the kavod [glory] that is raised through converts and ba'alei teshuvah , who are made through Toras Chesed [Torah taught for the sake of teaching others]. When one merits yirah , one merits shalom — peace = completeness ( sheleimus ). "Where there is fear, there completeness is found." Through this one merits prayer: "a woman who fears Hashem — she shall be praised." § 2 — The Whole Loaf = Yirah = Completeness When one must bless HaMotzi and break the bread, one must seek a whole loaf ( shalem ). The whole = yirah = the root of completeness. The essential yirah approaches a person during eating (as explained in LM II:7 ). The berachah itself is through yirah : only through yirah can one truly praise Hashem — "a woman who fears Hashem — she shall be praised." The essential tikkun of eating = drawing shalom by completing yirah through raising kavod via making ba'alei teshuvah and converts. Eating extracts holy sparks from food. These sparks = souls that fell and became mixed. Raising them through proper eating with a berachah and heartfelt intention = making ba'alei teshuvah and converts — for converts and ba'alei teshuvah are also sparks and souls raised from where they fell. Through holy eating, Hashem's kavod rises (as in LM I:67 ): "the table of kings — the King of Glory." Therefore yirah comes during eating — because the yirah is completed through the rise of kavod from sparks extracted through eating. Therefore: seek a whole loaf = yirah = completeness. § 3 — The Mystery of Breaking: Birur after Birur Every thing in the world must be clarified ( birur ) through clarification after clarification until reaching its ultimate completeness. This is seen most clearly in eating: the food arrives through many clarifications — first plowing and sowing, then reaping, then separating wheat from chaff and straw, then grinding and sifting from bran, then kneading into dough, dividing, baking. At every stage, what seemed complete before is incomplete relative to the next stage. All this is because the original fall of the sparks was through the sin of eating — Adam's eating from the Tree of Knowledge. Therefore food requires the most clarifications: "by the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread." Before each clarification, the thing is in the aspect of palga [half/incomplete] — because of the soiled garments ( begadim tzo'im ) still clinging to it. As explained in LM I:14 on the teaching of Rabbah bar bar Chanah: "at the meeting-point of the head, it cast a palga and blocked the Yarden" — souls still far from holiness are called palga because they are still clothed in soiled garments that block them like a river. "Remove the soiled garments!" — only by stripping these garments can the obstructions be removed. Even when bread is whole and fit for the blessing — it still lacks its ultimate completeness . The final clarification occurs during eating itself: within the body, the food is ground, refined, and purified until the finest essence rises to sustain life, and the waste becomes literal refuse. This is the ultimate stripping of the soiled garments — and it only happens inside the person. Therefore the Sages were so careful about the breaking of the bread: one blesses on the whole (= yirah = completeness of the previous clarification), then immediately breaks it (= beginning the ultimate clarification through eating). Through the breaking, one must intend to raise the bread from palga to ultimate sheleimus — stripping the good from the soiled garments completely, so that the life-force rises pure and the waste is expelled. § 4 — Rav Ashi and Menasheh: "Where Do You Break HaMotzi ?" The Gemara ( Sanhedrin 102b): Rav Ashi said, "Tomorrow we will begin with our colleague [Menasheh, discussing his sins]." Menasheh appeared in a dream and asked: "From where do you break HaMotzi ?" Rav Ashi could not answer. Why did Menasheh choose precisely this question? Because avodah zarah [idolatry] is called "vomit and filt

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Likutay Halachos seuda betzias hapas 4  Devarim HaNohagin BSeudah Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Likutay Halachos Seuda Betzias Hapas Devarim Hanohagin Bseudah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Devarim HaNohagin B'Seudah — Halachah 4 Part 1: §§ 1–12 — Rosh HaShanah through Sukkos Based on "Tisha Tikkunin Yakirin" ( LM I, 20 ) Herein is explained the mystical dimension of Rosh HaShanah, Yom Kippur, the Ten Days of Teshuvah, Sukkos, the Four Species, Hoshana Rabbah, Shemini Atzeres, and Simchas Torah. § 1 — Rosh HaShanah: Revealing the Holiness of Eretz Yisrael All our service during these holy days — from Rosh HaShanah through the ten days of teshuvah , erev Yom Kippur, Yom Kippur itself, Sukkos, the four species, through Shemini Atzeres — is to reveal the holiness of Eretz Yisrael , so that we merit to come there. Rabbainu said when he taught this awesome Torah: "Whoever wants to be a true Jew — to ascend from level to level — it is impossible except through Eretz Yisrael ." He also said: "The main thing is when one merits to win the battle and come to Eretz Yisrael " — then one is called "a mighty warrior." Before arriving at Eretz Yisrael : "let not the one girding boast like the one removing." The holiness of Eretz Yisrael is revealed on Rosh HaShanah: "the eyes of Hashem your G-d are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year." In the Arizal's kavanos : on Rosh HaShanah the nesirah [cutting/separation] of Malchus begins, continuing until Yom Kippur. In the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkos, inner and surrounding chasadim are drawn. On Shemini Atzeres, Knesses Yisrael (= Malchus ) unites with her Beloved in love — the essential joy of Israel. All of this is the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , for Malchus = Eretz Yisrael = "a woman who fears Hashem." The essence of Malchus is to reveal His kingship to all: "and so, place Your fear, Hashem our G-d, upon all Your works… rule over the entire world in Your glory… let every creature know that You formed it." We conclude: "King over the whole earth, the holy King, the King of judgment." All this = revealing Malchus = revealing Eretz Yisrael 's holiness. For His kingship is primarily revealed there — Yerushalayim and the Bais HaMikdash : "great is Hashem, and greatly praised, in the city of our G-d." "Whoever dwells in Eretz Yisrael is like one who has a G-d; whoever dwells outside — like one who has none." On Rosh HaShanah eve we say "Mizmor L'Dovid — the earth is Hashem's" — beginning with the holiness of Eretz Yisrael (as Rashi explains), and ending with: "the King of glory shall enter." § 2 — Drawing Torah Through Mercy: Moshe's Error at the Rock To reveal Eretz Yisrael 's holiness, one must draw Torah — and one merits Eretz Yisrael through the Torah one draws. But one cannot enter until the obstructers — the slanderers of the Land — are subdued. Their subjugation depends on the renewal of Torah; the renewal of Torah depends on the additional holiness above. The essential principle from LM I, 20 : One who wishes to draw illuminations of Torah must pour out his prayer before Hashem in supplication. Before the teaching, he must pray as a pauper begging for a free gift — not relying on his own merit. Though his mateh oz [staff of strength from his good deeds] is aroused, it is not for self-glorification but for subduing the evil among the assembly. Before Hashem himself, he stands as a poor beggar, relying only on rachamim . This was Moshe's error. Hashem told him: "Take the staff" — to take the power of his merit for subduing the evil among the assembly . Then: "Speak to the rock" — speak gently, pour out prayer as a pauper. "Before their eyes" — connect with the souls of the assembly during the act. But Moshe used his staff's power for the Torah itself — drawing Torah by force, not through mercy and supplication, not connecting with the souls. Therefore the angels born from that Torah could not receive power from Edom [Esav's spiritual force] to subdue the obstructers. Edom answered: "you shall not pass through me." Moshe could not enter Eretz Yisrael . Through his passing, Moshe's soul added holiness above — rectifying what was lacking. This entire teaching is explained in LM I, 20 . § 3 — Rosh HaShanah: The Time of Gathering, Drawing Torah for Eretz Yisrael This is what we work to rectify on Rosh HaShanah — the time of gathering for all Israel, assembling around the tzadikim . We draw Torah to reveal Eretz Yisrael . The tzadikim teach Torah on Rosh HaShanah; those gathered where no tzadik teaches draw the Torah's holiness through the shofar — the aspect of Matan Torah given with the shofar 's voice. We say: "You were revealed…" — recalling Matan Torah . The shenah [sleep/dormita] in the kavanos = removal of the mochin so the Malchus can be "sawed off" and rebuilt. This means removing one's own merit — standing before Hashem without relying on one's good deeds, empty-handed. "There is no poor man except in da'as " — we remove our da'as , standing as paupers. This is what we say at the

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Masa Umasan 4 Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Masa Umasan Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Masa U'Masan 4 Part 1 — Sections 1–5 The matter of business dealings. One should be careful not to enter into a partnership with idolaters, etc., on account of: "And the name [of other gods] you shall not mention; it shall not be heard," etc. (As explained there in Orach Chaim, Siman 156) Based on the Torah [teaching]: "And it was after these things…" etc. ( Likutay Moharan I, 76 ) — see there, the entire Torah [teaching]. It is explained there that histakulus [gazing / contemplative looking] is an aspect of ohr hayashar [direct light] and ohr hachozer [returning light] , etc. And this is the aspect of: "For Hashem is exalted, yet He sees the lowly, and the haughty He knows from afar" (Psalms 138:6) , etc. And through histakulus , a kli [vessel] is formed — that is, boundary and time . For before one sees the thing, it is without boundary. And through the histakulus — by seeing the thing and it becoming engraved in one's mind — through this, a boundary is made for it, etc. And this is the aspect of the virtue of bitachon [trust in G-d] . For bitachon is an aspect of histakulus , an aspect of: "The eyes of all look hopefully to You" (Psalms 145:15) . And through this, one draws down the shefa [influx / sustenance] and livelihood — for the hashpa'ah [Divine flow] descends from Above constantly, except that it is without boundary and time. And it could be that what one needs now might come to him only after many years. But through bitachon — which is an aspect of histakulus toward Hashem, blessed be He — through this, one makes a vessel for the hashpa'ah , that is, boundary and time, so that the hashpa'ah should come at the time it is needed. And this is [the meaning of]: "The eyes of all look hopefully to You, and You give them their food in its time " (Psalms 145:15–16) . For through the histakulus with bitachon toward Hashem, blessed be He — the aspect of "the eyes of all look hopefully to You" — through this: "and You give them their food in its time " — "in its time" specifically, meaning in the aspect of boundary and time, for the histakulus makes a vessel, as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of the virtue of drawing close to tzadikim [righteous individuals] . For they create boundary and time so that the engagement in Torah and avodah [service of G-d] should be done properly, according to one's level, within boundary and within time. This is what King David, peace be upon him, prayed: "My soul thirsts [for You]… When shall I come and appear before the face of G-d?" (Psalms 42:3) . "And appear" — specifically — that the avodah should be in the aspect of seeing , meaning in the aspect of vessel and boundary and time; see there all of this well. For although this Torah [teaching] is from the language of the chavairim [companions, who transcribed it] and was not written well at all, nevertheless, one who examines and studies it carefully will find there, too, wondrous foundations and novel insights. For every single utterance that came forth from the mouth of Rabbainu [Rebbe Nachman], of blessed memory, is exceedingly deep and awesome. § 1 And this is the aspect of "conducting business dealings with emunah " (Shabbos 31a) . For the primary purpose of business dealings is to draw down the aspect of the power of sight , which is the aspect of His hashgachah [Providence] , blessed be He — that it should be drawn upon us in completeness, in the aspect of re'iyah [seeing] , which is the aspect of ohr hayashar and ohr hachozer . Through this, a vessel is made for the shefa , so that it should come at the [right] time, as mentioned above. For all business dealings are only completed through two people who conduct business with one another — this one gives that one money or a certain item, and his fellow gives him in exchange a different item. And through this, the aspect of ohr hayashar and ohr hachozer is made: for each one extends his flow to his fellow — which is the aspect of ohr hayashar [direct light] — and afterwards he in turn receives from him — which is the aspect of ohr hachozer [returning light]. And this is the aspect of re'iyah , through which specifically the hashpa'ah is drawn down within boundary and time, as mentioned above. Therefore, in truth, the primary drawing down of the flow of livelihood is only through bitachon , which is an aspect of histakulus — the aspect of ohr hayashar and ohr hachozer — through which one makes a vessel, namely, boundary and time, so that the hashpa'ah should be drawn down in boundary and time, and the livelihood should come to him at its proper time and moment. And the fact that one needs to engage in some form of business dealings and commerce is also only for this purpose — to draw down the aspect of the power of sight, the aspect of ohr hayashar and ohr hachozer , through the business dealings, as mentioned above, so that through this the shefa should come in boundary

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Masa Umasan 4 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Masa Umasan Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Masa U'Masan 4 Part 2 — Sections 6–12 § 6 And this is the aspect of the Omer of barley, the aspect of Sefiras HaOmer [the Counting of the Omer] — in order to draw down the shefa within boundary and within time. And this is the aspect of the receiving of the Torah on Shavuos . For the Torah is an aspect of the power of sight, an aspect of tanta" ( te'amim , nekudos , tagin , osiyos ) [cantillation marks, vowels, crowns, letters] , an aspect of "Beraishis" [In the beginning] , as is explained elsewhere. And therefore, we stay awake the entire night on Shavuos — in order to rectify the eyes , which are the power of sight. And through this, we are saved from karais [spiritual excision] , which is the aspect of: "Let their end be to be cut off" (Psalms 37:38) . For in their case [the wicked], the ohr hachozer is severed from the ohr hayashar , because they do not direct the light of their eyes in a straight and focused manner, etc. This is the aspect of: "Watch the innocent and see the upright, for the end of that man is peace" (Psalms 37:37) . And for this reason, on the night of Shavuos , when we stay awake, we recite the beginning and the end of every sidra [Torah portion] and of every book [of Scripture]. For "the end of a matter is better than its beginning" (Ecclesiastes 7:8) . Because all beginnings are difficult, and the conclusion is even more difficult. And therefore: "A mitzvah is only called by the name of the one who completes it" (Sotah 13b) . And: "One who begins a mitzvah is told: 'Finish it!'" (ibid.) — for they need to say to him "finish it," because one needs to be strengthened regarding the completion more than anything, since the completion is the most difficult. And this applies both in the general sense regarding all of Israel, and also to each individual person — both in the entirety of his service [of G-d] and in the specifics of every individual mitzvah and every act of service. And this is the aspect of the dispute of Korach against Moshe — that he dressed them in garments that were entirely techailes [blue wool] , etc. [see below, § 14] . And for this reason, we eat dairy foods on Shavuos in the morning, in the aspect of: "His eyes are like doves by streams of water, bathed in milk , sitting upon fullness" (Song of Songs 5:12) — "upon fullness" — the fullness of the world. That is, the aspect of complete hashgachah [Providence]. And this is the aspect of: "The first of the firstfruits of your land you shall bring to the House of Hashem your G-d; you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk" (Exodus 34:26) . And this is what is brought [in the Talmud] that the primary argument with which Hashem, blessed be He, deflected the angels — who did not want the Torah to be given to Israel, saying that it should be given to them — the primary rebuttal was through the mitzvah of basar b'chalav [meat and milk]. For He, blessed be He, said to them: "Did you not eat meat and milk at the [home of] Avraham their father?" (Shabbos 88b) . For the prohibition of basar b'chalav [meat in milk] is a great novelty. For it is forbidden to cook meat in milk — even a kid in its mother's milk, from which it nurses and is nourished and from which comes all its vitality. And the kid itself is permitted to eat. And the milk itself is permitted. Nevertheless, it is forbidden to combine them together. All of this indicates that it is impossible to comprehend the ways of His conduct, blessed be He — and upon this depends the primary receiving of the Torah. And let us return to explain a little: § 7 For the primary receiving of the Torah depends on the emunah of hashgachah pratis [faith in individual Providence]. For then the concepts of mitzvah and transgression, reward and punishment, are applicable — for nothing is hidden from Him and nothing is concealed from His eyes. And He, blessed be He, chooses Torah and practical mitzvos that are performed in this physical world from physical things. But one who denies Providence, G-d forbid, denies the entire Torah. And this is a well-known matter that is self-evident and requires no elaboration. And therefore, the entire Torah is an aspect of eyes — the aspect of "Beraishis" [ בראשית ], which is the beginning of the Torah. [The Zohar teaches:] "There is ראשי [ raishei — 'heads,' i.e. the three colors of the eye]; there is בת [ bas — 'daughter,' i.e. the pupil, the bas ayin ]" — which are the three colors of the eye and the pupil. For the primary essence of the entire Torah is the aspect of eyes, the aspect of seeing and Providence. That is: we believe in His individual Providence — that He, blessed be He, watches, gazes, sees, and supervises constantly over each and every thing in particular. As it is written: "From the place of His dwelling He watches over all the inhabitants of the earth" (Psalms 33:14) . And through the fact that we believe in His Providence, blessed be He, we dire

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Masa Umasan 4 Part3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Masa Umasan Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Masa U'Masan 4 Part 3 — Sections 13–18 § 13 And this is the aspect of what one needs to strengthen himself exceedingly, exceedingly, at the time of the completion of the mitzvah and the service that he has begun. And as our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "One who begins a mitzvah is told: 'Finish it!'" (Sotah 13b) . And: "A mitzvah is only called by the name of the one who completes it" (ibid.) . And as we see with our own senses — that the completion is exceedingly, exceedingly difficult and heavy. For the beginning is very difficult, and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "All beginnings are difficult" (Mechilta, Yisro) . And after the beginning, things proceed somewhat in order. But afterwards, when one reaches the completion, it is exceedingly difficult and heavy. And therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, needed to admonish greatly regarding the completion, as they said: "One who begins a mitzvah is told: 'Finish it!'" etc., as mentioned above. That is, according to what was explained above: for the completion is the aspect of acharis [end]. And one does not merit to bind the acharis to the raishis [beginning] — which is the ultimate purpose of all the mitzvos and acts of service, as mentioned above — unless he merits to complete the mitzvah in its entirety . And therefore the ba'al davar [the adversary / the evil inclination] incites himself greatly over this. And therefore one must strengthen himself greatly to complete the mitzvah and the service that he has begun. For every mitzvah and act of service in particular has a beginning and an end. And the mitzvah is not complete until one finishes it. For example: when one needs to have tefilin written for him — behold, at first one needs toil to prepare the hide and the parchment with all the necessary preparations. And afterwards, to prepare the ink, and to write upon them according to law and regulation. And afterwards, when one finishes writing all the parshiyos [Torah sections] — as long as even a single letter is missing from them, they are not in the category of tefilin at all, until one finishes writing all the parshiyos in their completeness. And afterwards, even when the parshiyos are already completed as they should be — nevertheless, even if one writes a thousand parshiyos and wraps himself in them from head to toe, he does not fulfill the mitzvah of tefilin . For it is impossible to fulfill the mitzvah of tefilin until one makes batim [housings] of leather, and inserts the parshiyos into them, and sews them with sinews specifically, and prepares them with straps, etc., and places them upon the arm and upon the head in their proper place specifically. And then, specifically, he has fulfilled the mitzvah of tefilin . It emerges: as long as the mitzvah has not reached its acharis and end — that is, its completion according to the law of the holy Torah — it is not a mitzvah at all. And so too with the mitzvah of tzitzis : even if one wraps himself in a tallis that is entirely techailes [blue wool], he does not fulfill [the mitzvah of] tzitzis until he hangs the tzitzis [fringes] on the corners of the garment. And so too with the mitzvah of mezuza : even if the house is full of holy books, one does not fulfill [the mitzvah] through that, until one affixes the mezuza by the doorpost. And similarly with all the mitzvos. For every single mitzvah has measures and boundaries according to the words of the holy Torah — that one needs to perform it in this specific manner, as was transmitted to us from the mouth of Moshe Rabbainu, peace be upon him. And specifically when one fulfills it as it should be, as was transmitted to us — then one merits to draw the light that is drawn through every mitzvah, to draw it from raishis to acharis , from the head of all levels to the end of all levels, until this world is included in its root, in the aspect of "the end of action [was] in the first thought." And this is the aspect of the ultimate purpose of the service of the Torah and the mitzvos — which is the aspect of complete Providence in ratzo vashuv [running and returning], as mentioned above. § 14 And this is the aspect of the dispute of Korach . As our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bamidbar Rabbah 18:3; Midrash Tanchuma, Korach 2) , that his dispute was that he asked: "A garment that is entirely techailes — is it obligated in tzitzis ?" [Moshe] said to him: "Yes!" He began to mock him: "A garment of a different type — a single thread of techailes exempts it. How much more so…" etc. And similarly, he asked: "A house full of holy books — is it obligated in a mezuza ?" etc. This is as mentioned above. For Korach denied the fundamental [principle]. And in truth, he challenged the entire Torah and did not want to believe that one can draw down His Providence and life-force upon us through the fulfillment of the Torah and mitzvos. For he fell into the heresy of the here

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Masa Umasan Halachos 1-2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Masa Umasan Halachos Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Masa Umasan — Halachah 1 COMPLETE FULL TRANSLATION Based on LM I:69 The root of nefashos is in wealth; masa umasan b'emunah ; the prohibition of partnership with idolaters Halachic framework : "Afterward he shall go to his business, etc. It is forbidden to enter into a partnership with idolaters, lest a [situation requiring an] oath arise, and he would transgress 'the name of other gods you shall not mention; it shall not be heard upon [your mouth],' etc." ( Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 155). Introduction The matter is as follows: It is explained in the words of Rabbainu zichrono livrachah (in Siman 69, Part I ) that the root of the nefashos [souls] is in wealth . The essential magnification of the shem [name] and the nefesh [soul] is through holy wealth ( ashirus d'kedushah ), for holy wealth is exceedingly lofty — see there. It emerges that holy money — which is Jewish money — is the aspect of shem [name] and nefesh [soul]. And the shem and nefesh of Israel is the aspect of the Name of Hashem, for His Name is joined with our name. This is the aspect of "Did you conduct your business dealings with emunah [faithfulness]?" — " b'emunah " specifically! For emunah is the aspect of the Name of Hashem — the aspect of "Hashem is One, and His Name is One" — which is the essence of emunah . Therefore one must conduct business with emunah , for the root of masa umasan [business] is embedded within emunah , which is the aspect of the Name of Hashem, since masa umasan and wealth are the aspect of shem as explained above. And "G-d made this corresponding to that." For money of the Sitra Achra is the opposite: it is the aspect of the name of other gods, for all forms of idolatry are embedded in money, as Rabbainu zichrono livrachah states elsewhere (in Siman 23, Part I ). The totality of Jewish money is the aspect of holy money, which is shem and nefesh , the aspect of the Name of Hashem as above. And the totality of idolaters' money is money of the Sitra Achra , which is the aspect of actual avodah zarah — the aspect of the name of other gods as above. Now it is well explained why our Sages zichronam livrachah forbade entering into partnership with idolaters on account of "the name of other gods you shall not mention," etc. For certainly one violates "the name of other gods," etc., when one enters into partnership with idolaters, because the root of the nefashos is in wealth. When one enters into partnership with idolaters, one links one's own nefesh and the nefesh of the idolater together, chas v'shalom , so that both are rooted together in one pool of money — the very place where the root of the nefashos resides, as above. Therefore one certainly violates "the name of other gods," etc., for the nefesh and money of the idolater — which is the root of his nefesh — is the name of other gods. And "go, say to him" [= depart from it!] — it has no right to be joined with Jewish money, which is the aspect of the shem and nefesh of Israel, in which the Name of Hashem is embedded. This is what our Sages zichronam livrachah said: "lest a [situation requiring an] oath arise." For a holy oath is the aspect of the Name of Hashem, as it is written: "You shall not take the Name of Hashem [in vain]," etc., and "you shall not swear by My Name [falsely]," etc. Therefore, wherever there is a dispute between two people and it is unknown to whom the money belongs, an oath is imposed between them. The oath clarifies the truth — to whom the money belongs. For the oath is the aspect of the Name of Hashem, which is the root of money (which is the aspect of shem , as above). Therefore through the oath, it becomes thoroughly clarified to whom the money belongs, since at its root, the money of each person is certainly well-clarified — no one can touch his fellow's [money] there at all. Therefore our Sages zichronam livrachah were concerned lest the idolater be required to swear an oath. For this is something likely — close to certain. For idolaters are full of falsehood in business, because their money — which is money of the Sitra Achra — is taken from the aspect of sheker [falsehood], which is avodah zarah — the aspect of sheker . Therefore they are always suspected of falsehood, as it is written: "whose mouth speaks vanity and whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood." Therefore certainly the idolater will be required to swear their oath — which is the aspect of other gods, for from there is the root of their money, from the aspect of avodah zarah , from the aspect of the name of other gods, which is the aspect of their false oath. Therefore it is forbidden for a Jew to enter into partnership with him, for Jewish money is holy money — the root of his shem and nefesh , in which the Name of Hashem is embedded, as above. See the discourse beginning "Whoever wishes to draw people close to Hashem," etc., where it is explained regarding the ve

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - neteylas yadaym and bet 6 subdivision - birchas pairos rayach 88 107
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Neteylas Yadaym And Bet Subdivision Birchas Pairos Rayach Likutay Halachos – Orach Chaim, Volume II Laws of Natilas Yadayim for a Meal & Betziyas HaPas Sub-category: Birchas HaPairos [Blessings over Fruits] Birchas HaPairos [Blessings over Fruits] 88 This corresponds to the [law] that one does not recite zimun [the invitation to communal grace after meals] over fruits, because fruits have no fixed status [ kevias seudah — the status of a fixed meal], only bread made from the five species [of grain], which alone satisfies and nourishes. As has already been explained in the Laws of Birchas HaMazon (in section 75), that the essence of birchas hazimun [the blessing of invitation] is the aspect of the revelation of ratzon [Divine will/desire], which is revealed at the time of eating specifically, through the generality [ kelaliyus ] of son and student [ ben v'salmid ] — which represents the totality of the worlds [ kelaliyus ha'olamos ] — which each person merits through the holy daas [divine knowledge/consciousness] of the tzadik , the true shepherd [ ha'ro'eh ha'emes ], who toils to gather in the dispersed of Israel, those who are very far from Hashem, to return them to holiness, etc. It is for this reason that the main birchas hazimun — which is the greatest revelation of ratzon — is when there is some gathering of Israel of at least three. And the primary [revelation occurs] when ten gather at one table, when the zimun is recited with [G-d's] Name, etc. — see there well. Therefore, birchas hazimun applies only to bread, but one does not recite zimun over fruits, because fruits have no fixed status — for it is known and already explained that the taste of all foods and their power to vivify a person is drawn only from the daas and chachma [wisdom], from which all vitality flows, as it is written, "The wisdom gives life" [Koheles 7:12] . And according to the portions of sparks of daas that Hashem drew into each and every food, so does it have the power to vivify and sustain a person — for through this his soul is bound to his body, which is the essence of life — which is the aspect of the totality of the worlds [ kelaliyus ha'olamos ], etc., as above. Therefore the primary [food] is bread, which alone satisfies and nourishes a person, because in bread is clothed the main totality of daas , which is the aspect of the remozim [allusions/hints] mentioned above. Therefore with bread, even though one does not feel in it as much sweetness of taste as in other fruits and foods, even so it surpasses all foods and is the basis of them all — because all the aspects of the sweetness of daas invested in all the fruits and foods are all included in bread, within which the above-mentioned remozim are hidden, which represent the totality of daas — and therefore in truth, within bread all the flavors of the world are hidden, as above. Therefore birchas hazimun — which is the shining of the illumination of ratzon [Divine will] in greatest measure — applies only to bread, because the main illumination of ratzon is revealed most greatly through the gathering of Israel — through which comes the main totality of the worlds, etc. And as explained above, this is the aspect of [the teaching] that we do not recite matters of holiness [ davar sheb'kedusha ] with fewer than ten. And the more a holy gathering of Israel gathers and occupies itself with magnifying, sanctifying, and blessing His blessed Name, the more the worlds are encompassed one within the other, and so too the illumination of ratzon shines more and more. And the truest gathering is through the Shepherd of Israel [ ro'eh Yisroel ], who encompasses within himself all the true tzadikim of every generation, who toils to gather Israel "like a shepherd tends his flock, with his arm he gathers" [Yeshaya 40:11] , etc., as above — for he toils at the settlement [ yishuvo ] of the world, which is to illuminate daas within Israel, and this is the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, who was a true compassionate one [ rachaman emes ], and he is the aspect of the true tzadik of every generation, etc. — as explained at the beginning of the Torah we are currently studying, "For He who has mercy upon them will guide them" [Yeshaya 49:10 — see Likutay Moharan I:1] — see there. And the main [instrument of] gathering is through the remozim [allusions] within daas — through which comes the main illumination of true intellect into the heart of each and every person, from the greatest to the smallest, in every place and level that he is, so that he may strengthen himself however he is able, to return from all the evil places that wish to push him there, G-d forbid, and to separate him from the holy gathering, G-d forbid. He must not listen to any [such] push in the world, but rather strengthen his hand in Hashem and stand on his feet with all his strength and hold fast with all his might to the holy gathering of Israel — through which he will never fall, for "Behold

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 1 When one comes to eat bread over which one recites the blessing of HaMotzi , he must wash his hands. (Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim, Siman 158) See the discourse: "And on the day of the firstfruits…" ( Likutay Moharan I, 56 ) § 1 For eating is the life of a person. And the primary power of life-force within the thing that is eaten is the aspect of the da'as [knowledge/awareness] and saichel [intellect] clothed within it — for within every thing there is wisdom. And through this, [food] has the power to give life to the soul of a person. And in particular, the eating of a Jewish person — which is only in order to give life to his holy soul, as it is written: "The righteous eats to satisfy his soul" (Proverbs 13:25) . It emerges that through eating one receives life-force — that is, wisdom — and gives life to the soul. And therefore [eating] is the aspect of the drawing of life and longevity into Malchus [Kingship] , for the nefesh [soul] is the aspect of Malchus . And therefore, the primary food consists of the five species of grain , for they are the aspect of da'as , as our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Every child that tastes the taste of grain…" (Berachos 40a) [begins to say "Father" and "Mother," i.e., develops da'as ], etc. And these five species of grain correspond to the five [aspects of] da'as , as Rabbainu [Rebbe Nachman] wrote. And therefore they are meizan zaynai [truly nourishing / satisfying] (Berachos 36a) . For the primary nourishment and satisfaction come from the da'as , as mentioned above. And because of their importance, [the Sages] established for them a blessing of their own, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said. And therefore, they ordained to bless HaMotzi with five words specifically — corresponding to the five [aspects of] da'as mentioned above. And even upon the five species of grain, one does not recite HaMotzi except upon what is specifically called lechem [bread]. But upon other foods made from them — such as pas haba'ah b'kisnin [grain-based snack foods, e.g. cake or crackers] and other types — one does not recite HaMotzi over them. For lechem [bread] is the aspect of da'as , the aspect of "bread from Heaven" that Rabbainu wrote about there. And as it is written: "Come, eat of my bread" (Proverbs 9:5) . And the primary [definition of] bread is what is called bread for the purpose of matza — meaning, [dough] that can come to a state of chimutz [leavening] , as the Magen Avraham cites there (OC 158) . For the primary da'as is the bread of matza , the aspect of "the cake that they brought out of Egypt," etc. — see there. And matza is only called [matza] when [the dough] can come to a state of leavening if it were left to sit — that is, when it is kneaded with water. For this is a principle: the sitra achra [the other side / forces of impurity] trails after holiness, and in every place where there is an abundance of holiness, there the sitra achra is found seeking a place to draw sustenance. And therefore, in a place where one sees the intensification of the sitra achra , one knows that certainly in that place there is great holiness. And therefore, one does not fulfill the obligation of matza except with [dough] that can come to a state of leavening. For then, specifically, it is the bread that is the aspect of da'as , the aspect of matza . And therefore, if one had not been careful to guard it well, it would certainly come to a state of leavening — which is the sitra d'mosa [the side of death] . For it [the sitra achra ] is found in the place where there is holiness, which is the aspect of da'as . For the primary holiness is da'as . And the key factor is when the dough is kneaded with water — which is the aspect of chasadim [kindnesses] , which is the aspect of da'as . And then it is called lechem , the aspect of "bread from Heaven," the aspect of da'as , the aspect of matza . And then it can come to a state of leavening, as mentioned above. And also, it must be specifically from the five species of grain, which are the aspect of da'as , as mentioned above. And therefore, one does not fulfill the obligation of matza except with the five species of grain. And therefore, one does not recite HaMotzi except upon such bread that is fit to be matza — for then it is the aspect of da'as , as mentioned above. And even though we eat chametz [leavened bread] throughout the year — nevertheless, since it was fit to be matza and is called lechem , it emerges that there is a clothing of holiness within it — namely, da'as — except that the da'as is in the aspect of concealment [ hastarah ], meaning that it became leavened. For chametz is the sitra d'mosa — the opposite of life and longevity — the aspect of the concealment of da'as . And therefore we are able to eat it, for we have the power to reveal the concealment and to restore it to da'as — since we ha

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 2 Based on the discourse of Rabbainu , may his light shine, ( Likutay Moharan I, 44 ) — concerning the clapping of hands, which serves to purify the air in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , through the power of the joints of the hands, through which the "power of His deeds" is aroused. For it is found in the words of Rabbainu , may his light shine ( Likutay Moharan I, 44 ), concerning the clapping of hands [ mechi'as kaf ] — that it serves to purify the air in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , through the ko'ach pirkin d'yadayim [the power of the joints of the hands] , through which the "power of His deeds" [ ko'ach ma'asav ] is aroused — for the primary holiness of Eretz Yisrael comes through this — see there. And through this, one is saved from confusing thoughts , which are the aspect of mabul [the Flood] , the aspect of bilbul [confusion] . And through drawing down the holiness of Eretz Yisrael , one is saved from the aspect of the mabul — for in Eretz Yisrael , there was no Flood — see there well. And this is the aspect of netilas yadayim before eating . For eating and prayer are one and the same aspect — that is, the aspect of beirurim [refinements / sortings of holy sparks] that are accomplished through prayer and through eating, as is brought [in the holy books]. And therefore, the primary holiness of eating is only in Eretz Yisrael , from where all the shefa is drawn — for Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of emunah . And all the beirurim are accomplished through emunah , as is brought. And as Rabbainu wrote (in the discourse "Vayaseiv" , Likutay Moharan I, 62 ) — that the refinement of foods is accomplished through emunah , in the aspect of: "and graze on emunah " (Psalms 37:3) . And this is accomplished through Eretz Yisrael , in the aspect of: "Dwell in the land and graze on emunah ." For there, they are nourished from emunah , through which all the beirurim [are accomplished]. And therefore, one must see to it that the shefa of one's eating is drawn from Eretz Yisrael , and that one's eating should be as if he is eating in Eretz Yisrael . And for this, one needs to join the hands together, to arouse the ko'ach pirkin [power of the joints], through which the "power of His deeds" is aroused — so that there should be made here the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , as mentioned above, for the matter of prayer — so that the beirur [refinement] should be done properly. And through this, the blemish of the Flood is rectified — which is rectified through Eretz Yisrael , as mentioned above. For eating in holiness is the rectification of the blemish of the Flood, which is the aspect of the sin of Adam HaRishon [the first man], through which good became mixed with evil. And this was itself the sin of the generation of the Flood — for "all flesh had corrupted its way" (Genesis 6:12) , etc. — and through this, good and evil became intermingled, as is brought. And one needs to refine [this mixture] every day. And the primary refinement is through prayer and eating. And therefore, the prayer needs to be in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael — where there was no blemish of the Flood, for there was no Flood there, as mentioned above. And therefore there, one rectifies the blemish of the Flood through the beirurim accomplished through prayer. And similarly, eating — which is also beirurim — needs to also be in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , to rectify the blemish of the Flood, as mentioned above. And therefore, one needs netilas yadayim — so that one can raise one's hands in the aspect of: "Lift up your hands in holiness" (Psalms 134:2) . For through this, the "power of His deeds" is aroused through the ko'ach pirkin of the hands — which is the aspect of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael , as mentioned above. For it is impossible to raise and join the hands without first washing them. For the hands are "busy" [ askaniyos ], and the primary hold of the sitra achra is at the tips of the fingers, as is brought. And in particular, the blemish of the Flood mentioned above — the primary damage of this blemish affects the hands specifically, in the aspect of: "Your hands are full of blood" (Isaiah 1:15) . And as long as one does not sanctify and purify the hands from the blemish mentioned above, it is impossible to raise them. As it is written: "And when you spread your hands, I will hide My eyes… your hands are full of blood" (Isaiah 1:15) . For one needs to raise the hands in holiness, in the aspect of: "Lift up your hands in holiness," as is brought. For then, through the holiness of the ko'ach pirkin of the hands, the holiness of Eretz Yisrael is aroused from the aspect of "the power of His deeds," as mentioned above. And therefore, the hands are purified through the pure waters of washing — for through this, one removes from the hands the aspect of the mayin hazaidonim [the malicious waters] , the waters of the

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 3 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 3 Part 2 — Sections 7–8 § 3 (continued) — The Vessel and the Medameh And therefore, the vessel needs to be complete . For the water symbolizes the da'as — the wondrous da'as that will be revealed in the future, in the aspect of: "And the earth will be full of the knowledge [ dei'ah ] of Hashem as the waters cover the sea" (Isaiah 11:9) . And the primary da'as is to know Hashem — that is, to know and believe that He, blessed be He, is the Sole Primordial One; He is the Former, He is the Creator [who creates] something from absolute nothing — that is, the emunah of the renewal of the world [ emunah d'chidush ha'olam ], as mentioned above, and as is explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. For through the da'as — the aspect of "and the earth will be full of knowledge" etc. — one merits the levels mentioned above, until one merits this emunah : namely, the emunah of the renewal of the world, which is the main thing, as mentioned above. And this da'as mentioned above — which is the aspect of water — it is impossible to attain and receive except through a vessel , which is the aspect of emunah , which is in the aspect of the medameh [the imaginative faculty] , as is explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. For the medameh is the vessel of the true da'as . For in truth, all the opinions of the entire world — even of the great philosophers and investigators — are all merely in the power of the medameh . For true da'as is only to know Hashem. And this, they have not even begun to attain or taste at all. For this da'as , no one merits except exceedingly great and awesome tzadikim , singular individuals of the generations. But we — we do not have the power to attain this da'as . And we need to strengthen ourselves only with emunah , which we merit through the refinement of the medameh — which is refined through our meriting to draw close to true tzadikim , as is explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. And therefore, these wicked apikorsim [heretics] — who do not want to rely on the da'as of the holy tzadikim , and who, in their loathsomeness and filth, immersed in all the desires, presume to investigate with their polluted intellect — therefore, in truth, their medameh is intermingled and confused, until they come to great heresies or false beliefs. For it is impossible to draw and receive from the holy da'as except through meriting to sanctify and refine the medameh through drawing close to true tzadikim . Through this, the medameh is refined. And then one merits complete holy emunah . For the primary emunah is in the medameh — for in what the intellect comprehends, one does not need emunah , as is explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. And this refined medameh , which is the aspect of emunah — it is the aspect of a vessel that draws and receives the waters of da'as . And this is hinted at in the Torah teaching mentioned above, where it is written at the end that all the titles and praises with which we describe Him, blessed be He, are all in the aspect of the medameh , etc. And this is the aspect of: "on our festival day" [ l'yom chagainu ], the aspect of: "and with the compass he gives it form" (Isaiah 44:13) , etc. — see there at the end. And this is the aspect of a vessel. For the plain meaning of the verse "and with the compass he gives it form" is said regarding the making of a vessel, as it is written there (Isaiah 44) : "He shapes it with planes and with the compass he gives it form," etc. And there, it speaks of the disgrace of false beliefs — of those who believe in idolatry, wood and stone, the works of human hands. And this is the aspect of vessels of the sitra achra — which are false beliefs, believing in wood and stone literally. But on the contrary, in holiness — the holy emunah in Hashem, blessed be He, which is in the aspect of the refined medameh , through which one merits to describe and praise Him, blessed be He, with fitting titles and praises as is proper — all this is the aspect of a vessel in the spiritual sense . For the titles and praises with which we describe and praise Him are vessels to receive the perception of His G-dliness — each one according to what he estimates in his heart. For in truth, "no thought can grasp Him at all" . Only through prayers and songs and praises — that is, titles and praises — which He, in His mercy, gave us permission to describe and praise Him with: through this, we have the power to draw upon ourselves the holy emunah , through which vessels are made to receive the perception of His G-dliness — each one according to what he estimates in his heart. And therefore, the vessel for netilas yadayim needs to be in completeness, without any blemish or deficiency — so that it can receive and contain the water, which is the aspect of the waters of da'as mentioned above, which is the da'as that

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 3 Based on the discourse "Vayehi mikeitz — ki merachamam yenahaigem" ( Likutay Moharan II, 7 ) — see there. Concerning what is written there, that through the inclusiveness of son and student, one merits the illumination of the Ratzon [Divine Will] at the time of eating, etc. § 1 And this is the aspect of netilas yadayim for a meal — so that the eating should be in the aspect of holy eating, in which the illumination of the Ratzon [Divine Will] is revealed at the time of eating. This is accomplished through the livelihood being drawn from the aspect of the hands that are in the Sea of Wisdom [ yam hachochmah ], etc. And therefore one merits the illumination of the Ratzon at the time of eating specifically — see there in the discourse mentioned above. And this is the aspect of netilas yadayim before eating. For through washing the hands and purifying them with water — through this, one draws upon them the illumination of the Ratzon from the Sea of Wisdom. And then the hands are included within the aspect of the waters of the Sea. For a revi'is of water is the aspect of a mikveh , as is brought in the poskim [halachic authorities] — that by Torah law, a revi'is purifies [like] a mikveh . And a mikveh is the aspect of a sea, as it is written: "And the gathering of the waters He called 'seas'" (Genesis 1:10) . And therefore, through the revi'is of water with which one purifies the hands — through this, the hands are included within the aspect of the Sea, that is, within the aspect of the Sea of Wisdom. And then, the primary eating and livelihood are drawn from these hands — for the primary livelihood is drawn from the hands that are in the Sea of Wisdom, as mentioned above. And then, when one merits to receive one's eating from there, then the illumination of the Ratzon is drawn and revealed at the time of eating — and this is the primary holiness of eating. And this is the primary purpose — to merit the illumination of the Ratzon mentioned above. For the Sea of Wisdom mentioned above — where the makifin [surrounding lights] shine, which are the aspect of the illumination of the son — and the student — this is the aspect of the illumination of the da'as of Moshe Rabbainu, peace be upon him, who illuminated this da'as , as is understood there in the discourse mentioned above. And the primary [purpose of] the da'as is to save and guard and extricate Israel from transgressions, G-d forbid — for this is the primary compassion toward Israel, the holy nation: for one who knows from where Israel is drawn, [understands] how they are utterly distant from sins, may the Merciful One save us, etc. — see there. And one who merits to illuminate the da'as in Israel and to guard them and save them from every sin and transgression — through this, the makifin mentioned above shine, the aspect of the Sea of Wisdom, from where livelihood is drawn from the hands that are in the Sea mentioned above. And through this, one merits the illumination of the Ratzon at the time of eating. It emerges that the primary illumination of the Ratzon is drawn through being guarded from transgressions — which is drawn through the da'as mentioned above, which is the aspect of Moshe, as mentioned above.
