And all the transgressions, G-d forbid — the primary damage they cause is in the aspect of the hands , as is understood in the words of Rabbainu , of blessed memory, elsewhere. As our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "And you will not come to the hands of a transgression" — "to the hands " of a transgression, specifically. And this is the aspect of "the sadness of the hands" [ itzavon yadainu ] that is said regarding the generation of the Flood, who rebelled against the Omnipresent. As it is written: "This one shall comfort us from our work and from the sadness of our hands" (Genesis 5:29) , etc. For the primary blemish — which is the aspect of sadness, the aspect of "and He was saddened in His heart" (Genesis 6:6) — affects the hands specifically, as is understood in the words of Rabbainu on the verse "and from the sadness of our hands" mentioned above, which is brought in the discourse "And on the day of the firstfruits" ( Likutay Moharan I, 56 ) — see there. For the primary blemish of all the transgressions affects the hands — which are the aspect of the totality of the entire Torah, the totality of the entire world. As Rabbi Elazar the Great said before his passing — he raised his two hands and said: "Woe for the two Torahs that are lost from the world" (Sanhedrin 68a) . And as it is written: "My hand also laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens" (Isaiah 48:13) . For the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world through the Torah — which is the aspect of the two hands. And therefore, the primary blemish, G-d forbid, reaches the hands. And then the hands are in the aspect of: "An

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 4 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 4 Part 2 — Sections 4–10, including Betzi'as HaPas § 4 — Why Water Purifies from All Impurities And for this reason, water purifies from all impurities . And it is impossible to enter into any holiness without water — such as the Kohanim in their [Temple] service. And similarly, in the morning upon rising. And similarly, before prayer and Torah study, one needs to immerse or wash one's hands with water. And similarly, all the ritually impure do not ascend from their impurity except through water. For water symbolizes the da'as of the renewal of the world. For water preceded all of creation — for the beginning of creation was water, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said. It emerges that the primary renewal of the world began from water. And therefore, there is the primary root of the da'as of the renewal of the world — through which the primary purification [is accomplished]. And only through this does one enter the service of Hashem. For this is the primary foundation of the holy emunah — to believe in the renewal of the world, in the aspect of: "In the beginning, G-d created the heavens" etc. — which is the beginning of the Torah. And this is the primary holiness and purity. For conversely, all the impurities are drawn from the zuhamas hanachash [contamination of the serpent], which brought death — from which the primary impurity [comes]. And the primary [aspect] of the contamination of the serpent is the heresy of those who deny the renewal of the world, G-d forbid. And therefore, water — which is the aspect of the waters of da'as mentioned above, through which the emunah of the renewal of the world is drawn — through this, [one achieves] all the purifications in the world. And it is impossible to enter any holiness or service except through water. For all holiness and all service of Hashem depend on this emunah of the renewal of the world — which one merits to draw upon oneself through purification in water, through immersion or washing, according to the law. For through purification in water, one draws upon oneself the aspect of the illumination of the waters of da'as that will be revealed in the future — through which one merits the emunah of the renewal of the world, which is the foundation of the Torah and of service, as mentioned above. § 5 — The Four Fasts, Tisha B'Av, and Shabbos Chazon And this is the aspect of the four fasts over the destruction of the Bais HaMikdash — which was caused by the sin of the spies, who wept on the night of Tisha B'Av , who blemished Eretz Yisrael — where the emunah of the renewal of the world is revealed. And they blemished this. Through this, the zuhamas hanachash — mezona d'gufa — intensified, G-d forbid, as mentioned above. Therefore one needs to fast, in order to subdue the mezona d'gufa . For when one merits complete emunah , one does not need to fast. For through emunah , the eating is in the aspect of mezona d'nishmesa — which is the aspect of the eating of upright Jews, the aspect of eating on Shabbos. For through emunah , the primary refinement of eating [is accomplished], as is explained elsewhere, in the aspect of: "and graze on emunah " (Psalms 37:3) . But because they blemished Eretz Yisrael and blemished the emunah , as mentioned above — therefore one needs to fast, to subdue the mezona d'gufa through the fast. And this is the aspect of Eichah [Lamentations] that we recite on Tisha B'Av . And this is the aspect of: " Eichah — how the gold has become dim" (Lamentations 4:1) . For the primary [subject of] the lamentations is over the passing of the true tzadikim — which is twice as [devastating as] the destruction of the Bais HaMikdash . And through this, we are now like "sheep that have no shepherd." For we do not know who the true tzadik is. And we need to cry out and search and seek: " Eichah ! Eichah ! [Where?! Where?!]" — [seeking] the true tzadik whose light has been darkened for us, for we do not merit to know of him. And this is: "how the gold has become dim" — the true tzadik , who is more precious than gold, has become dim, and his light has been darkened for us. And as our Sages, of blessed memory, said — that Yirmiyahu was lamenting "how the gold has become dim" over the passing of the tzadik Yoshiyahu. And so too, in every generation, it alludes to the passing and concealment of the light of the true tzadik of the generation. And this is: "how the gold has become dim" — that his light has been darkened for us, and we do not merit to benefit from his light. And it is not enough [that his light is hidden] — but our sorrow is compounded by more grief still. For "the fine gold has changed" (Lamentations 4:1) — the true tzadik , who is likened to fine gold, has had his light so thoroughly darkened from Israel that the truth itself has been completely changed. For "they call evil good and good evil" (Isaiah

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 4
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 4 Based on the Torah teaching "Tik'u Tochachah" ( Likutay Moharan II, 8 ) — see there the entire Torah teaching from beginning to end. And the principle, in a great brevity necessary for our subject: That one needs to subdue the mezona d'gufa [nourishment of the body] , which is the aspect of the heel of Eisav . And to strengthen the mezona d'nishmesa [nourishment of the soul] . And this is merited through drawing down the voice of the melody and song that will be aroused in the future — which is the aspect of the voice that waters the garden, through which all the awe and the fragrances grow — which are the mezona d'nishmesa , in the aspect of: "Your voice I heard in the garden, and I was awed" (Genesis 3:10) . For this voice is the aspect of "a river goes out of Eden to water the garden" (Genesis 2:10) , etc. And it is the aspect of "The voice — the voice is the voice of Yaakov" (Genesis 27:22) — which subdues the heel of the sitra achra , in the aspect of: "and his hand was holding the heel of Eisav" (Genesis 25:26) , etc. — see there very well. And to merit this voice is through the prayer in the aspect of judgment of the ba'al ko'ach [the man of power] — through which one extracts from the sitra achra all the holiness and all the waters of da'as that it swallowed. And the da'as of holiness is revealed, in the aspect of: "For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem, as the waters cover the sea" (Isaiah 11:9) . And through this, converts are made and His glory, blessed be He, is revealed. And through this, prophecy is drawn down. And through prophecy, the medameh [imaginative faculty] is refined. And through the refinement of the medameh — through this, the primary strengthening of the holy emunah . And then one merits complete emunah in the renewal of the world [ chidush ha'olam ] — which is impossible to attain through da'as alone, but only through emunah . And this is the primary foundation of the holy emunah — to believe that Hashem, blessed be He, created the world yaish mai'ayin hamuchlat [something from absolute nothing] . And through this emunah , one merits the renewal of the world of the future. And then the world will be conducted in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael . For the primary holiness of Eretz Yisrael is through the aspect of "the power of His deeds He told to His people" (Psalms 111:6) , etc. — meaning, through the emunah of the renewal of the world, the aspect of "In the beginning, G-d created the heavens" etc. As Rashi explains there — that for this reason [the Torah] opened with "Beraishis" : because of "the power of His deeds He told" etc. — so that they could conquer Eretz Yisrael . It emerges that the primary holiness of Eretz Yisrael is through believing in the renewal of the world — that Hashem, blessed be He, created the world something from nothing, as it is written: "In the beginning, G-d created" etc., as mentioned above. And the primary holiness of Eretz Yisrael is that there His Providence, blessed be He, is revealed, in the aspect of: "The eyes of Hashem your G-d are constantly upon it" (Deuteronomy 11:12) , etc. And in the future, when the entire world will be conducted in the aspect of Eretz Yisrael , as mentioned above — then the entire world will be conducted only through Providence alone, and nature will be completely nullified. And then the song of Providence and wonders will be aroused, etc. And this song is the aspect of the voice mentioned above that waters the garden — through which one merits the mezona d'nishmesa and one subdues the mezona d'gufa , in the aspect of "and his hand was holding the heel of Eisav" etc. — see all this there very, very well, for they are long and deep matters, deeper than the sea; there is nothing comparable to them. § 1 And this is the aspect of netilas yadayim before the meal. For we, the children of Israel, the holy nation — we need to sanctify our eating with great holiness, until our eating is in the aspect of mezona d'nishmesa , in the aspect of: "The righteous eats to satisfy his soul" (Proverbs 13:25) . For this eating is from the side of Yaakov Avinu — who subdues the mezona d'gufa , which is the side of Eisav, the aspect of the heel of Eisav, as mentioned above. And therefore, before eating, one needs to purify and sanctify our hands with water — so that we should have the power through this to subdue the mezona d'gufa and to strengthen the mezona d'nishmesa — so that our eating should be in the aspect of mezona d'nishmesa . And this is the aspect of netilas yadayim for a meal. For through the mitzvah of washing the hands with water — through this, we draw down the waters of da'as mentioned above, which emerge through the prayer of the ba'al ko'ach mentioned above, through which one merits all the levels mentioned above — until one merits to draw down the river that goes out of Ed

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Netilas Yadayim LSeudah 6 1-9
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Netilas Yadayim Lseudah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Netilas Yadayim L'Seudah U'Betzi'as HaPas 6 Based on "Ki Merachamam Yenahaigem" ( LM II, 7 ) . Already partially explained in Halacha 3. [Halacha 5 is included in Hilchos Bais HaKnesses 5.] § 1 — Hands as Remazim : Including Left in Right For one needs to purify the hands specifically before eating. For all of man's service in this world is l'achlela smola bimina — to include the left within the right — as is understood from the Holy Zohar in many places. For the entire hold of the sitra achra is from the sitra dismola [side of the left]. And the primary service for which man came into this world is to subdue the sitra achra until the left is included within the right. And right and left are the aspect of the upper worlds and lower worlds , in the aspect of: "My hand also laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens" (Isaiah 48:13) . Earth and heavens are the aspect of the lower and upper worlds. And this is the aspect of body and soul, chomer [matter] and tzurah [form]. And this is the aspect of this world and the World to Come. For it is all one concept: the body relative to the soul is in the aspect of this world, matter, the lower worlds, the left. And the soul is in the aspect of the World to Come, form, the upper worlds, the right. And the main thing is that all these aspects — which are the entirety of the worlds, the upper within the lower and the lower within the upper — should be included together , as is explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. And through eating , the soul is joined with the body. For eating gives life to a person — the soul gives life to the body through eating. For so Hashem, blessed be He, created in His will: that specifically through eating, the vitality of the soul should be drawn to the body. When the soul separates from the body, G-d forbid, that is death. Therefore, Adam HaRishon's first commandment concerned eating. For his primary rectification depended on eating. And Hashem, blessed be He, desired that all his eating should be only from the illumination of the Ratzon , drawn from yam hachochmah — from which the primary root of livelihood and holy eating [derives]. Through this, the primary completeness of the joining of upper and lower worlds is accomplished — the comprehensions of Ayeh [Where?] and Melo [Fullness], as explained in the Torah teaching. Through this, the primary inclusiveness of left within right. And there is the root of the two hands — through which heaven and earth were created. They are the aspect of the remazim [hints] in yam hachochmah — the contemplation inherent in the holy study that cannot be explained by mouth explicitly ; one completes them with the hands, which are the aspect of remazim . And through this specifically, the comprehensions of the son and the student — Ayeh and Melo — are included together. For the comprehension of G-dliness is exceedingly exalted — "no thought can grasp Him at all" ; only each one according to what he estimates in his heart. And the main thing is the inclusiveness of Ayeh and Melo — which cannot be grasped in the mind and heart except through the aspect of remazim , the aspect of hands in yam hachochmah . From there descend all the holy studies and all contemplation in Torah and yirah — all of which it is impossible to understand from one's rav in completeness except through remazim , which are the aspect of hands. For even in the wisdoms of Torah in the revealed dimension — in p'shatim in Gemara, the commentary of Tosafos — it is impossible to understand the essence and the sweetness of the p'shat and the chidush except through the rav completing [the explanation] for the student with his hands , which are remazim . As we see with our senses: the rav explains the p'shat to his students with the movements of his hands. How much more so in the pathways and counsels of the service of Hashem — where the Adversary attacks a person with schemes without number, every day, nearly every hour and moment — such that it is impossible to withstand except through the Torah we received from our Rabbainu , of blessed memory, and the main thing is the remazim within the Torah. And therefore, one needs to search and seek greatly for a true Rebbe who received from a true Rebbe , and to speak with him time after time — in order to understand the remazim that he hints with his hands: how far to strengthen oneself, etc. etc. And all of this is drawn through holy eating, drawn from the hands that are the remazim in yam hachochmah , where the illumination of Ratzon shines. And therefore, one needs to purify the hands specifically before eating — the purification through water drawn from yam hachochmah . And then one merits that eating in holiness has the power to join soul with body — the inclusiveness of upper and lower worlds, the inclusiveness of left within right, as mentioned above. § 2 — Morni

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Seudah 1-2-3  and Betzias HaPas 3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Seudah And Betzias Hapas Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim Hilchos Seudah — Halachah 1 Wine Exempts All Beverages Based on "Ha'i man d'azil l'minsav" ( LM I, 29 ) Wine, Blood, and the Rectification of Da'as See the teaching "One who goes to marry…" ( LM I, 29 ), where it is explained that the rectification of all the damim [bloods] is achieved by elevating the moach [brain/mind]. From there, a whiteness flows into all the bloods. The berachah on every item serves to strengthen and rectify one's nefesh . Through this, one can rectify the nefesh clothed within the food. This is why our Sages forbade eating before prayer, deriving it from: "You shall not eat upon the blood" — "do not eat before you pray for your blood." "For the blood is the nefesh " — one must pray first to rectify his blood and nefesh . Then he can eat and elevate the nefashos clothed in the food. Prayer consists of songs, praises, blessings, and thanksgivings — through these the nefashos are rectified. For the nefesh is the aspect of dibbur [speech], and all nefashos clothed in everything are aspects of letters and speech. The tikkun of speech is through praising the tzadikim and blessing Hashem — the Tzadik of the world. This is also the berachah on each item — blessing and thanking the Tzadik of the world, rectifying the nefashos that are aspects of speech. The Tikkunim state: berachah is from the side of Imma Ila'ah — "to bring blessing to your house" — for there the blood is purified and becomes milk = the rectification of the nefashos . When one blesses over wine, the da'as is greatly elevated: "if one merits — it becomes a head" [= expanded mind]. Through the berachah = "meriting" = purifying the blood. Therefore one need not bless again on other beverages : since the da'as has been rectified and elevated through the wine and its blessing, the nefashos (= damim ) are automatically rectified — for the rectification of the damim depends on the da'as . Wine is so significant that one must bless on it even during a meal — bread does not exempt it. Bread too derives its importance from da'as — hence it exempts the entire meal. But wine, whose da'as is even greater, is not exempted by bread. We bless HaTov V'HaMeitiv on a change of wine — for all good depends on da'as : "also without da'as , the nefesh is not good." Wine = da'as ; where there is da'as , there is good. ✦ ✦ ✦ Hilchos Seudah — Halachah 2 Bread Establishes Its Own Blessing Based on "Chanukah V'Hoda'ah" ( LM II, 2 ) Blessings on Food: Including This World in the World to Come The essence: hoda'ah [thanksgiving] is the aspect of the World to Come — for the World to Come is to thank and praise and know Him. Through this, the dibbur is perfected = lashon hakodesh . Through this, the holiness of Shabbos is drawn into the six weekdays. Through this, the simple unity is revealed — that all diverse actions flow from the One. This is Birchas HaNehenin — the obligation to bless before every enjoyment. One must attach his thought to the World to Come and separate from this world entirely — "fortunate is one who derives no benefit from this world." For every necessity we take from this world (eating, drinking, etc.), we bless — thereby including and elevating these worldly things into the World to Come . When we bless Hashem for a food, that food becomes a vehicle of praise and thanksgiving = the World to Come aspect. The six weekdays (= this world, a mixture of good and evil) are sanctified by Shabbos (= the World to Come). Through blessing over the diverse things of this world — each with its different appearance, taste, and scent — we reveal that all these diverse actions flow from the simple One who created them. This revelation of unity from diversity is exceedingly precious to Him. Specific Blessings Are Greater Than General Ones Now it is perfectly clear why specific blessings are more valued than general ones. The more specifically one blesses — the more the simple unity is revealed from diverse and particular actions. She'hakol [the general blessing] does not reveal the unity from particular diversity as powerfully as Borei Pri HaGafen [a specific blessing on wine]. The more particular the action, the more precious is the revelation of His unity through it. The importance of each food depends on the da'as clothed within it — "wisdom gives life to everything." Where more da'as is clothed, it is more important and merits a more specific blessing. Da'as = the World to Come (= knowing Him, thanking Him). The more da'as , the more one grasps the simple unity. Bread and Wine: The Pinnacle Bread = da'as : "come, eat of my bread." Therefore it is the most important — establishing its own specific blessing. Only the five species of grain are called lechem = the hei of da'as . Bread accompanies the Korban Todah — and todah [thanksgiving] is the World to Come: "all sacrifices will be nullified except the todah " — in the future, only thanksgiving remains. Wine t

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis Halachah 4 Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Halachah 4, Part 1 (§§ 1–9) And in it will be explained the matter of Rosh HaShanah and the Ten Days of Teshuvah, Yom Kippur, Sukkos and the Four Species, Hoshana Rabbah, Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah Based on LM I:65 ( "Vayomer Boaz el Rus" ), see there the entire Torah from beginning to end § 1 And this is the aspect of Tefilas Arvis that Yaakov Avinu, peace upon him, established — he who is the choicest of the Avos . And it is the first prayer of all the three prayers of the day, for the day follows the night, and first comes night and then day, as explained in the words of our Sages of blessed memory. It emerges that Tefilas Arvis is the first of the three prayers. For the essential perfection of prayer is specifically through the bitul [self-nullification] by which one is included in the aspect of "it is entirely one, entirely good." Through this one merits to make one unity out of the entire prayer. And when one stands at the end of the prayer, one will still remember the first word of the prayer etc. — as explained in the Torah mentioned above. For when a person stands to pray, he walks in the Supernal Field and gathers blossoms and flowers, roses and beautiful grasses etc. And immediately when he utters the first letter etc., how much more so when he completes one word — the word seizes the soul from which the speech emerges and embraces and grasps the soul with immense love, and does not allow the soul to proceed further etc. But this is not the perfection of prayer, for one must complete the entire prayer and then say additional songs, praises, supplications and requests etc. Therefore the essential perfection of prayer is only when one merits to make one unity out of the entire prayer. Meaning: even when one proceeds from this utterance and speaks other utterances, nevertheless one will never forget the first utterance. And even when one stands at the end of the prayer, one will still remember even the first utterance of the prayer. Until even in the last word of the prayer one will still be standing in the first word of the prayer — for it is entirely one etc. See there. And this one merits only through meriting to gaze upon the tachlis [ultimate purpose], which is entirely one, entirely good etc. See there. And to gaze upon the tachlis is impossible except through bitul , through closing one's eyes completely — meaning one must shut one's eyes from the vision of this world completely, until one comes to the ultimate bitul . And then one will be included in the tachlis , which is entirely one, entirely good. And through this one will merit to make one unity out of the entire prayer — which is the essential perfection of prayer as mentioned above. See there, all of this, well. And it is explained there that this is the aspect of what is embedded in human nature: that when one has great suffering, G-d forbid, one shuts and closes one's eyes very forcefully. For there, when one gazes upon the tachlis , one sees that there is no suffering or evil in the world at all. For everything is for good. For the ultimate purpose of suffering is very great good. But it is impossible to gaze upon the tachlis except through closing the eyes etc. For when one wishes to see something far from one's eyes, one must focus the vision etc. Similarly, when one wishes to gaze upon the tachlis , which is very far from human eyes, one must close one's eyes completely and press them with one's finger — meaning one must close one's eyes from the vision of this world completely. And then specifically one can gaze upon the tachlis , which is entirely one, entirely good, and there all suffering is entirely nullified, as mentioned above. Therefore it is embedded in human nature to close one's eyes forcefully during severe suffering — in order to flee from the suffering. For through closing one's eyes during suffering, through this one is included in the tachlis where all suffering is nullified, as mentioned above. But it is impossible to remain there, for one would be nullified from existence, and necessarily the bitul must be in the aspect of ratzo v'shov [running and returning]. And when one returns from the bitul , the suffering returns and intensifies even more, G-d forbid, etc. But afterward, one cools the suffering through the Torah that one draws from the aspect of the bitul . For through the bitul one is included in the aspect of "entirely one, entirely good," and there one sees that all suffering is great good. And through this, joy is drawn upon him. And then, when one returns from the bitul and a reshimah [trace] remains from the bitul , the joy becomes a vessel for receiving the Torah. And one merits attainment of the Torah through the light of the shining and sparkling of the reshimah from the bitul , which illuminates and shines into the mind that has become ve

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis Halachah 4 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Halachah 4, Part 2 (§§ 10–17) Based on LM I:65 ( "Vayomer Boaz el Rus" ) § 10 And we are engaged in this tikun of the aspect of bitul mentioned above — which is the aspect of teshuvah , as mentioned above — from Rosh HaShanah until Yom Kippur , which are the Ten Days of Teshuvah . For it is impossible to repair in a single day, lest it be in the aspect of excessive light. Therefore one must repair through many tikunim, gradually. [As is brought in the Writings of the Ari"zal: that on account of Adam HaRishon's sin, one must delay and tarry in the tikun of Malchus — which is the tikun of the worlds — from Rosh HaShanah until Shemini Atzeres .] And this is the aspect of the Ten Days of Teshuvah from Rosh HaShanah until Yom Kippur . And the essential aspect of the bitul is on Yom Kippur . And this is the aspect of all the five afflictions that one accepts on Yom Kippur . For then one closes one's eyes from the vision of this world completely and accepts upon oneself all the afflictions. Therefore one merits then to be included in Olam HaBa , in the aspect of bitul mentioned above. For Yom Kippur is the aspect of Olam HaBa , as is known — the aspect of departure and bitul toward the tachlis , which is Olam HaBa . Therefore the Kohen Gadol enters then into the innermost sanctum, the Kodesh Hakodashim — where the essential aspect of bitul toward the tachlis resides. Therefore on Yom Kippur is the essential perfection of prayer, for one prays five prayers then, which is not found on any other day. For then is the essential aspect of the bitul , through which is the essential perfection of prayer — that one can pray many prayers by making one unity out of the entire prayer, as mentioned above. § 11 And this is the aspect of Tefilas Ne'ilah that one prays on Yom Kippur — for then is the essential completion of the tikun that is performed on Yom Kippur . For the essential tikun through the bitul that one merits on Yom Kippur is to bind the entire prayer together, to make one unity out of the entire prayer — that even when standing at the end, at the last word of the prayer, one will still be standing at the first word of the prayer, as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of Ne'ilah of Yom Kippur . For then is the completion of the tikun, which is the aspect of ne'ilah [locking/closing] — meaning one locks and closes and binds the entire prayer together, meaning one makes one unity out of the entire prayer. This is the essential tikun that one merits on Yom Kippur through the bitul that one merits then in perfection, as mentioned above. And this is why at the end of Tefilas Ne'ilah one says: "Shma Yisra'el, Hashem Elokainu, Hashem Echad." Meaning: we are included then in the ultimate oneness where it is entirely one — whether chesed , whether judgment, all is one etc., as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of "Hashem Hu HaElokim" that one says then — meaning that all is one, whether chesed or judgment, which is the aspect of "Hashem Hu HaElokim." This is the essential perfection that one merits through the bitul , as mentioned above in the Torah mentioned above. And this is the aspect of receiving the Torah that one receives on Yom Kippur , for then the last Tablets were given — meaning the aspect of the Torah that one receives from the light of the shining of the reshimah from the bitul when it is in the aspect of v'shov etc., as mentioned above. § 12 For the essential bitul is completed in perfection on Yom Kippur . And then one accepts all the afflictions — this is the aspect of closing one's eyes from the vision of this world completely. For even though on Rosh HaShanah , from the intensity of the judgment that is aroused, one nullifies oneself toward the tachlis etc. as mentioned above — nevertheless it is impossible then to complete the tikun in perfection. For it is impossible to merit the aspect of bitul in perfection immediately at the beginning of teshuvah , lest it be in the aspect of excessive light. As is explained in the Writings [of the Ari"zal]: if Adam HaRishon had not sinned, he could have completed the tikun immediately in a single day. But now, after the sin, it is impossible to repair in a single day etc., see there. Therefore even though one nullifies oneself on Rosh HaShanah etc. as mentioned above, it is impossible to remain there long in the aspect of bitul , lest it be in the aspect of excessive light etc. Therefore one must immediately draw the tikun drawn through the mitzvah of shofar — which is the aspect of the awakening of sleep, in the aspect of v'shov : we return from the bitul and draw the light of the shining and sparkling of the reshimah etc. — which is the aspect of the power of receiving the Torah etc., as mentioned above. But because the tikun has not yet been completed in perfection, one cannot complete the aspect of re

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis Halachah 4 Part3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Halachah 4, Part 3 (§§ 18–28) Based on LM I:65 ( "Vayomer Boaz el Rus" ) § 18 And this is the aspect of: "Hashem sat [enthroned] at the Flood" — which is said at the end of the seven sounds that Dovid spoke over the waters, and which are the aspect of the sounds of the Giving of the Torah that was given with sounds, as explained in the seforim : that this psalm speaks of the Giving of the Torah. For the Flood waters that came upon the world then — this was drawn from the aspect of excessive light, which causes the Breaking of Vessels, from which all judgments and troubles derive, G-d forbid. Meaning: the judgment then was exceedingly intense on account of their evil deeds, and they needed a bitul in perfection until they would merit to nullify the judgment. And then they would have drawn the attainment of Torah — which is the aspect of waters — from the reshimah that remains from the bitul , as mentioned above. But because they did not merit this and did not arouse themselves to teshuvah — which is the aspect of bitul , as mentioned above — therefore what should have been the aspect of the waters mentioned above, which are the aspect of the attainment of Torah, became instead the aspect of the waters of the Flood, because they had no vessels to receive the light, on account of the corruption of their deeds. Therefore it was, in their regard, in the aspect of excessive light — from which all judgments derive — and these are the waters of the Flood. Therefore our Sages of blessed memory said, in truth, on the verse "and the rain was upon the earth" : that had they aroused themselves to teshuvah , they would have been rains of blessing and generosity. Meaning, as mentioned above: had they merited teshuvah — the aspect of bitul , as mentioned above — they could have received the attainment of the waters of Torah, which are the aspect of rains of blessing and generosity, in the aspect of "a rain of generosity You poured down, O G-d" — which is said regarding the Giving of the Torah. But because they did not merit teshuvah , what should have been the waters of Torah, the rains of blessing, became a Flood for them, as mentioned above. And this is what Rashi explains on the verse "for with them He judges the peoples" — regarding rain: a parable of a baker etc. — that all punishments are through water and all blessings and bounty are through water, in the aspect of "He gives food abundantly." Meaning, as mentioned above: the rains and waters are drawn from the aspect of the waters of da'as and the supernal attainments that are compared to water, as it is written: "for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem, as the waters" etc. Therefore there are two aspects in them — for good and for the opposite — depending on the recipients. For one who merits through his deeds to repair good vessels — he merits the attainment of the waters of da'as through this. And the opposite for the opposite, as mentioned above. § 19 And this is the aspect of what Noach merited afterward — through the offerings he attained to bring, as mentioned above — he merited that [Hashem] gave him the sign of the rainbow as an eternal protection, in the aspect of "I have set My bow in the cloud." For the rainbow is the aspect of gunin nehirin [luminous colors], the aspect of the light of the shining and sparkling drawn from the reshimah of the bitul — through which is the essential sweetening, as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "and I shall see it, to remember an everlasting covenant" — "to remember" specifically, the aspect of the remembrance mentioned above — the aspect of Rosh HaShanah , Yom HaZikaron , which is the aspect of the light of the reshimah , as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of the sounds of the holy shofar , whose mnemonics are Kuf-Shin-Tav [= Keshes , rainbow], as is brought. This is the aspect of the sign of the rainbow, which is the aspect of the light of the shining of the reshimah — which is the aspect of the shofar , as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of the reddening of the face of the one who blows [the shofar ], which is drawn from the supernal lights, as is brought. This is from the aspect of the light of the shining of the reshimah , from which all the lights and splendors and Sefiros derive. And this is the aspect of the sound of the holy shofar , the aspect of the luminous colors of Keshes , as mentioned above. § 20 And this is the aspect of: "and it was, after seven days, that the waters of the Flood were" etc. — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: that He gave them a delay of the seven days of mourning for Mesushelach the righteous. For it is explained in the Torah mentioned above, at its beginning, regarding the Ba'al HaSadeh who is engaged in the tikun of the Field — which is the tikun of the souls etc. — that this Ba'al H

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis Halachah 4 Part4
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Halachah 4, Part 4 (§§ 29–39) Based on LM I:65 ( "Vayomer Boaz el Rus" ) § 29 Therefore one studies Sefer Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy] on the night of Hoshana Rabbah . For Mishneh Torah is the aspect of binding the light of the reshimah well, in the aspect of a seal within a seal, so that we never forget Him. For the Torah is the aspect of a seal — for through it one binds the light of the reshimah in our hearts well. For the essential knowledge of Hashem is through the Torah, which is drawn from the light of the reshimah , which enters and is bound in the heart through the holy Torah, as mentioned above. But even the Torah itself one must review well, so as not to forget it, so that we do not forget Him, G-d forbid. And this is the aspect of the great warning that Moshe Rabbainu, peace upon him, warned us: "only guard yourself and guard your soul exceedingly, lest you forget the things... and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life, and you shall make them known to your children and your children's children." And this is the aspect of Mishneh Torah — the aspect of a seal within a seal. For the Torah is the aspect of a seal, being called the Torah of Truth, which is the aspect of a seal — for "the seal of the Holy One blessed be He is truth." Therefore at the beginning of the Torah, Emes [truth] is imprinted, as it is written: " B ereishis bara E lokim" — the final letters spell Emes — which is the aspect of a seal. And Mishneh Torah is the aspect of a seal upon a seal. For Moshe Rabbainu, peace upon him, repeated and reviewed the Torah before Israel in order to bind the seal of Torah in the heart of Israel well, in the aspect of a seal upon a seal. Therefore most of the words of Mishneh Torah speak of this matter: Moshe warning Israel with many warnings upon warnings, that they should remember well all that Hashem did with them — all the great and awesome things that their eyes saw. As is clear throughout the entire Sefer Mishneh Torah , and especially at its end, which is Shiras Ha'azinu . For all the words of this song are so that the Torah will not be forgotten from the mouths of our seed, as it is written: "this song shall testify before him as a witness, for it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his seed." Therefore one recites Mishneh Torah on the night of Hoshana Rabbah , for the entire essence of Hoshana Rabbah is to bind the light of the reshimah well in our hearts, in the aspect of a seal within a seal, so that we never forget Him — which is the aspect of Mishneh Torah , as mentioned above. § 30 And this is the aspect of Sefer Tehilim that one recites then. This is the aspect of the tikun of prayer that one merits at the completion of the tikun on Hoshana Rabbah , as mentioned above — which is the aspect of Tehilim , which encompasses all prayers, songs and praises. For we now merit to say many songs and praises, all of which are encompassed in Sefer Tehilim . For we merit through the tikunim mentioned above to make one unity out of the entire prayer — through which one can speak many prayers, which are the entire Sefer Tehilim composed by Dovid HaMelech, peace upon him, who saturated the Holy One blessed be He with many songs and praises, all encompassed in Sefer Tehilim . And this is the aspect of the ten "Halleluyah" s with which Sefer Tehilim concludes — "Halleluyah" at the beginning and "Halleluyah" at the end. This is the aspect of the tikun of prayer: when standing at the last word of prayer, one is still standing at the first word, as mentioned above. This is the aspect of "Halleluyah" at the beginning, "Halleluyah" at the end — for it is all one, as mentioned above. Therefore one says these ten "Halleluyah" s every day in Pesukei d'Zimrah before prayer, for the essential tikun of prayer is through making one unity out of the entire prayer, that when standing at the end of the word etc. — which is the aspect of the ten "Halleluyah" s: "Halleluyah" at the beginning, "Halleluyah" at the end, as mentioned above. § 31 And this is the aspect of Simchas Torah . For the essential drawing of Torah from the reshimah , as mentioned above, is through joy — which is the vessel for receiving Torah, as mentioned above. Therefore, after all the tikunim mentioned above are completed at the end of the days of Sukkos , on Hoshana Rabbah , we then celebrate Simchas Torah . For this is the essential completion of the tikun: we merit to draw the aspect of receiving the Torah in perfection, and the essential receiving is through joy, as mentioned above. Therefore we then complete the Torah and immediately begin [again], binding and joining its end with its beginning. This is the aspect mentioned above of the tikun of prayer: when standing at the end, at the last word, one is still standing at the beginning, at the first word. For it is

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis Halachos 1-3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Halachos Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Halachos 1–3 Halachah 1 Tefilas Arvis Reshus, v'ha'idana kav'uha alaihu chovah [The evening prayer is optional, but nowadays they have established it upon themselves as an obligation] Based on what Rabbainu wrote in the teaching "Pasach R' Shimon" ( LM I:60 ): that through yirah [fear/awe of Hashem] one merits great wealth, and through this wealth one comes to hisbonenus [deep contemplation] of the Torah. For through yirah one subdues the aspect of "charm is false and beauty is vain" — see there well. Now, Yaakov is the aspect of yirah , as the Zohar states: "b'yirasecha" [in Your awe] — in the merit of Yaakov, who said "how awesome [ nora ]." Therefore he was not afraid at all of the aspect of "vain beauty." Therefore we do not find regarding Yaakov that his marital union was ever forbidden to him, even when he descended to Egypt — on the contrary, Hashem assured him: "I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also surely bring you up" etc. For Yaakov's bed was complete, and he guarded the Bris exceedingly, and he had no hold or fear from the aspect of "vain beauty." All this was because he merited the aspect of yirah , which subdues the aspect of "vain beauty" as mentioned above. On account of this, Yaakov merited exceedingly great wealth, as it is written: "and you shall spread out to the west and to the east" etc. — meaning an inheritance without boundaries, meaning the aspect of all the wealth of the world. For all the Avos merited great wealth according to their level of yirah , according to how much they subdued "vain beauty." But Yaakov, who was the perfection of yirah and merited to subdue entirely the aspect of "vain beauty" as mentioned above — therefore he merited the ultimate wealth, meaning all the wealth of the world, an inheritance without boundaries as mentioned above. Therefore Tefilas Arvis is reshus [optional]. For Tefilas Arvis is the aspect of Yaakov, for he established it, and he is the aspect of yirah as mentioned above, through which one merits great wealth, through which one merits the great hisbonenus mentioned above. Therefore it is reshus , for when one merits this hisbonenus , then there is no obligation to pray. For this hisbonenus is the aspect of the attainment of R' Shimon bar Yochai, who merited this. Therefore he was exempt from prayer, as our Sages of blessed memory said. For this hisbonenus is the aspect of "his Torah is his craft" — meaning that all his craft and wealth is solely from the Torah, the aspect of the chips of the Tablets from which Moshe became wealthy, as our Master, our Teacher and our Rebbe wrote there — see there. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: "they only taught [the exemption from prayer] regarding someone like R' Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues, whose Torah is their craft" etc. According to the simple meaning this is puzzling, for are there not also now people who have no craft at all and only engage in Torah — how much more so in the days of the Shas! But the essential thing depends on the hisbonenus mentioned above, which depends on wealth. Therefore it is called "their Torah is their craft" as mentioned above. Therefore Yaakov specifically established Tefilas Arvis . For then, at night, the time is more conducive to attainments and hisbonenus , as it is written in the Shivchei HaBa'al Shem Tov that most Torah chiddushim are merited at night. And as Rabbainu wrote ( LM I:52 ) that at night it is more conducive to bitul [self-nullification] — see there. Also, the night is the aspect of wealth, the aspect of "she tasted that her commerce is good; her lamp does not go out at night." For wealth comes from there, as is implied in several places in the words of Rabbainu — for one who examines there. Therefore Tefilas Arvis is reshus as mentioned above. But nowadays they have established it upon themselves as an obligation. For now, one does not merit this level of attainment even at night, and therefore it is an obligation to pray as mentioned above. Therefore in the evening one recites two berachos before Krias Shma and two after it. But in the morning one recites only three berachos — two before it and one after it. For Arvis , which corresponds to Yaakov who merited an inheritance without boundaries — the aspect of "and you shall spread out to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south" — and corresponding to this one recites four berachos before and after Krias Shma , corresponding to the four directions of the world. For one merits then the inheritance of Yaakov, an inheritance without boundaries. But at Shacharis one recites only three berachos , corresponding to three directions of the world's structure, for the north is lacking. There, the Sitra Achra overpowers — the aspect of "from the north evil shall break forth" etc. For Shacharis corresponds to Avraham, w

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas Arvis LM I 49  - end of Mincha 7 from 82 to end
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Arvis Lm I End Of Mincha From To End Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas Arvis [Laws of the Evening Prayer] Based on LM I:49 ( LaShemesh Ohel Bahem ) §§ 82–96, plus Rashay Perakim Continuation of Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 7 § 82 — Yaakov Established Tefilas Arvis : Prayer Even in Total Darkness The three Avos revealed His G-dliness and Malchus in the world — each through prayer. Avraham established Shacharis : the dawn-light of Ain Sof . But Adam failed to contract it — he gazed where he had no permission (Tikunai Zohar), flawed his thought, damaged his prayer. Even after his teshuvah , and even through subsequent tzadikim (Noach, Mesushelach, Shem, Eiver), none worked to reveal His Malchus to the world until Avraham — the first to repair the contractions, revealing G-dliness on earth (Rashi: through him He became "G-d of the earth" ). Avraham began the tikun of prayer (the essential revelation of Malchus ). Yitzchak added Minchah : when the mochin withdraw, only a reshimu remains — prayer for strengthening at the time da'as departs. But Yaakov, choicest of the Avos , added Arvis : after the sun has set entirely, in the darkness of night (= total withdrawal of mochin ). He repaired the tikun of prayer even then — so we can reveal His Malchus even from utter darkness. "Even darkness is not dark to You; night shines like day." Yaakov's bed was complete — he fathered all of Israel. But he foresaw through ruach hakodesh that they would sin. He therefore strengthened and repaired Arvis : that even one who fell into total darkness (= the prolonged exile = "darkness upon the face of the deep" = "He placed me in darkness" ) could draw the tikun of prayer (= teshuvah = revelation of Malchus ). He perceived that the root of all corruption derives from excessive light → Breaking of Vessels → absence of is'arusa d'l'sata . Each person must contract the light and guard from bad thoughts. Yaakov merited tikun of thought (= tikun of the Bris ) more than all the Avos : his bed was complete ( raishis ono ). From his immense holiness he could descend to the depths of every Jew's fall in every generation until ikvesa d'Meshicha . As Rabbainu taught: the greater and holier the tzadik , the lower he can descend to work on their tikun. Yaakov specifically repaired Arvis — in the time of total darkness. Even then: "no good will is ever lost." Every movement, every good point one detaches from bad to good — the tzadik (= Yaakov) gathers it into the holy structure. No matter what happens between the good points — strengthen to snatch more. The tzadik raises the is'arusa d'l'sata from the lowest places: the lower the source, the more precious the arousal. Through this, Yaakov builds the Third Bais HaMikdash (which will never be destroyed) — through Israel returning to Hashem by the tzadik 's power. § 83 — The Bais Midrash = the Third Bais HaMikdash , Built in Yaakov's Merit All tikun through the Mishkan / Bais HaMikdash (= the Batai K'nesiyos and Batai Midrashos of Israel = mikdash m'at ). The essential: the Bais Midrash named after the true tzadik of each generation (§§68-69). The Midrash (Eichah): "every great house" = the Bais Midrash of R' Yochanan ben Zakkai (called "great" — encompassing all the holiness of 481 Batai Midrashos in Yerushalayim). Through the Bais Midrash 's holiness: every good point snatched even from utter darkness is gathered by the tzadik into the Mishkan / Bais HaMikdash he builds constantly. Through this: one becomes part of the nation, included in the holy gathering — building the Third Bais HaMikdash (in Yaakov's merit, never to be destroyed). Our Sages: the first two were in Avraham and Yitzchak's merit; the third in Yaakov's. Yaakov repaired Arvis when he "encountered the place" ( "this is none other than the house of G-d" ) — tikun of the Third House: prayer even from darkness (= teshuvah = Malchus revealed). § 84 — Is'arusa d'l'sata : "If Hashem Wanted to Serve Himself, He Wouldn't Need You" All tikun through is'arusa d'l'sata . Hashem desires that we specifically serve Him from this world. As Rabbainu said to his followers: "if Hashem wanted to serve Himself, He wouldn't need you." Yet it is hard — the evil inclination expands, especially against those entering avodas Hashem ( "he stretched his hand against the great" ). Necessarily: help from above — yet all is from Him ( "who preceded Me that I should repay?" ). Still, some arousal from below is needed. This is unknowable: "the wonders of the Perfect in knowledge." Therefore every arousal is exceedingly precious. "Open for Me like a needle's eye." Immediately upon arousal: is'arusa d'l'ala follows — "whoever comes to purify is assisted." This is the essence of the yichudim made through prayer: uniting is'arusa d'l'sata with d'l'ala . This is what Yaakov perceived when he "encountered the place" (= the Bais HaMikdash ). Our Sages: why didn't the place stop him when he passed by? Because

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 3
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 3 Based on LM I:66 ( Vihi Na Pi Shnayim ) Introduction — The Spirit of Mashiach and the Opening of the Hands Halachah : The time of Minchah is after six hours. Based on what Rabbainu zichrono livrachah writes in the teaching " Vihi Na Pi Shnayim B'Ruchacha Ailay " ( LM I:66 ): there is an aspect of charon af [fierce anger], and one must sweeten and clarify the smoke of the charon af so that it becomes the aspect of ruach aviri [an airy spirit] — the spirit of Mashiach . Before it arrives at the aspect of the hands, it is the aspect of "before existence" [ kodem hahavayah ]. The essential existence is when this spirit arrives within the hands. Initially the two hands are one — the aspect of "before Creation." One must bring from potential to actual — opening and cutting the hands so there is a right hand and a left hand. This is the aspect of Creation — bringing from potential to actual. They are the two spirits — the pi shnayim [double portion] mentioned above: ruach d'l'aila [the spirit above] and ruach d'l'sata [the spirit below]. The aspect of the two Yuds — a Yud at the beginning and a Yud at the end — in the two Names [ Y-AKDONK-Y ], with six letters in between, the aspect of pesach [opening]: "You open Your hands [ yadecha ] — Your Yuds " — through the Vav (= the opening), the hands (= the Yuds ) are opened and divided. Then it is the aspect of Creation — bringing from potential to actual. See all this there well. § 1 — The Order of the Day: Night, Dawn, Morning, and Minchah This is the aspect of the order of the day. At night, in darkness — "when deep sleep falls upon men and the masters of judgment awaken" — this is the aspect of charon af . The charon af (= the smoke) must be clarified: "smoke rose in His anger." This is accomplished through the smoke of the korbanos , which ascended at night to subdue and sweeten all the masters of judgment (as brought) — clarifying and repairing the smoke of the charon af through the smoke of the korbanos . The smoke went out toward the north (as brought) — where all the masters of judgment and anger reside: "from the north evil shall open forth" — the aspect of anger: "remove anger from your heart and remove evil from your flesh." Through this, an abundance of sustenance is drawn: "from the north gold shall come" — when the anger of the north side is sweetened, wealth and sustenance are drawn from there (as Rabbainu writes in the above teaching; see there well). Then the smoke of the charon af is repaired and clarified, becoming a holy ruach aviri — the spirit of Mashiach . This is the north wind that blows upon David's kinor [harp] at midnight — the revelation of the kingdom of Mashiach (= the kingdom of David), revealed at midnight. It is a northern wind — revealed specifically from the north, from the clarification of the smoke and anger in the north. At midnight is the beginning of the revelation of the spirit of Mashiach . But it is still night and dark — the spirit has not yet reached the aspect of existence, the hands, until daylight. At dawn, the spirit is revealed in the aspect of the hands: "let there be light" and "there was light" — right hand and left hand. Initially: "the earth was void and chaos and darkness" — the aspect of anger, judgment, charon af . From there specifically the spirit of Mashiach is clarified: "the spirit of G-d hovered" — "this is the spirit of Mashiach " (Zohar, Vayechi 240) — drawn from the clarification of the darkness and smoke. Then: "G-d said: let there be light, and there was light" — the two hands (as brought). The spirit is drawn into the hands — then the essential existence: "let there be light." "G-d saw the light, that it was good — and He stood and stored it for the future" — this light will not be revealed until Mashiach comes and the World to Come, for this light is the spirit of Mashiach . "G-d separated between the light and the darkness; G-d called the light 'day'" — afterward He brought from potential to actual: the two spirits are revealed (= the two Yuds : beginning of thought and end of action = day and night, as known). At first they were intermingled (being one); afterward they were separated and opened. See the above teaching well. Then comes the essential Creation. "There was evening and there was morning" — the essential beginning of Creation and the revelation of the hands through the aspect of "He separated." At daylight (= "let there be light" and "there was light" ), the spirit of Mashiach is revealed in the hands. Therefore we then don tefillin — where the kingdom of Mashiach is revealed in the knot of the tefillin (as brought). The tefillin of the head and of the hand (arm) are the aspects of right and left — the hands, the two Yuds . The essential tefillin are during Krias Shma and tefilah : Krias Shma is the Daled of Echad (= th

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 4
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 4 (§§ 1–14) Based on LM I:64 ( Bo El Pharaoh ) Introduction — The Chalal HaPanui , Emunah , and Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah : Our Sages warned especially about Tefilas HaMinchah : "one should always be careful with Tefilas HaMinchah ." They also warned not to begin anything close to Minchah : "one should not sit before the barber close to Minchah without first praying; one should not enter a bathhouse..." Based on the teaching " Vayomer Hashem el Moshe: Bo el Pharaoh, ki Ani hichbadti es libo " ( LM I:64 ). See the entire teaching there and understand well — these are exceedingly deep and wondrous matters. The principle: all the wisdoms, difficulties, heresies, and confusions for which there is no answer — all come from the chalal hapanui [the Vacated Space], from which Hashem contracted His G-dliness, as it were, for the purpose of creating the world (without this, creation would have been impossible — everything would have been One). Since these inquiries and difficulties come from the chalal hapanui (from which He contracted His G-dliness), it is certainly impossible in any manner to understand these inquiries or resolve these difficulties. For if one could understand and resolve them, one would find Hashem there as well — but in truth, one cannot find Hashem there through inquiries from the chalal hapanui (He contracted His G-dliness from there for the world's creation). Therefore regarding these inquiries it is said: "all who enter her shall not return" — it is forbidden to enter these inquiries at all, for one will certainly never understand them or find a resolution. One can only rely on emunah alone — believing in Hashem with complete emunah without any inquiries whatsoever. In absolute truth, Hashem is certainly found there too, even in the chalal hapanui — certainly nothing exists without His vitality. But it is impossible to understand this in any way until the future — when the contraction of the chalal hapanui will be understood: how He contracted the radiance of His G-dliness from there, yet He is found there nonetheless. In this world it cannot be understood at all — one must rely solely on emunah . (This is why Israel are called Ivriim — because they have emunah ; see there.) Only the exceedingly great tzadik (the aspect of Moshe) can enter there — and he must enter to raise from there all the souls that fell there. Through the song that this exceedingly great tzadik sings, he raises them: "then Moshe sang" ; "you shall come, you shall gaze from the peak of Amanah [faith]." See all this there well. § 1 — Each Day Is a New Creation; Minchah = the Contraction Before the Next Day This is the aspect of Tefilas HaMinchah — toward evening as the day turns, "then harsh judgment prevails" (Zohar). Every day is the aspect of the world's creation: "in His goodness He renews the act of Creation every day." Each day a unique creation is created — each day an aspect and measure in itself: the revelation of the days and the midos . The essential revelation of Creation (= the days and midos ) was through the chalal hapanui (= the contraction). Therefore each day, before one day departs and the next enters, there must be something like the moment of the world's creation: the contraction of the chalal hapanui is renewed — through which the next day is revealed as a new creation. Every night precedes the day: "there was evening and there was morning" — the world's creation: "first darkness, then light." The contraction of the chalal hapanui is the aspect of night and darkness (= withdrawal of light). Night precedes day because the contraction must precede the creation (= the revelation of light). This is: "the advantage of light comes from darkness" — the essential revelation of light is from the darkness (= the contraction). This is also the aspect of the moon's diminishment: "two kings cannot share one crown" — there would be no room for creation. "Go and diminish yourself" — the contraction of light, making room for the world's creation, governed through the moon (= malchus ). § 2 — Why There Is No Krias Shma at Minchah : Only Emunah Without Da'as Every day, after midday, the sun begins to diminish — until midday it grows brighter, then afterward contracts and diminishes so it does not spread excessively (it must diminish for the world's creation — renewing the next day's creation, impossible without the contraction of light). The contraction is the intensification of judgment — all heresies, all difficulties of the philosophers and deniers, all come from the chalal hapanui . As long as idolatry (= heresies and apikorsus ) exists in the world, charon af is in the world. All good and chesed is Hashem's light: "Hashem is good to all." Whoever removes Hashem's light from himself through inquiries and difficulties — removes all good, and judgments

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 5
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 5 (§§ 1–9) Based on LM II:22 ( Anavah — Humility) Introduction — True Humility vs. Mochin D'Katnus The matter of Tefilas HaMinchah : Based on what Rabbainu zichrono livrachah writes ( LM II:22 ) regarding humility [ anavah ]: in the matter of submission and humility, the world errs greatly — for how much do we exert ourselves in tefilah to leave mochin d'katnus [contracted consciousness] and enter mochin d'gadlus [expanded consciousness]! If so, certainly this [mere self-abasement] is not the trait of humility as the world supposes. § 1 — Minchah : Sweetening the Mochin D'Katnus at Their Root This is the aspect of Tefilas HaMinchah . The essential work of man is to leave mochin d'katnus and enter mochin d'gadlus . Man's essential service is to break and subdue the evil inclination and its cravings — all the power of the evil inclination and cravings derive from mochin d'katnus , from which all judgments take hold and the evil inclination's essential power derives (as explained in Rabbainu's words many times). Therefore: "a person transgresses only if a spirit of folly enters him" — all sins and flaws come through the withdrawal of da'as that derives from mochin d'katnus . As explained in the teaching " Tik'u Tochachah " ( LM II:8 ): the desire for adultery (which encompasses all desires) derives from mochin d'katnus . Man's essential work is to leave mochin d'katnus and enter mochin d'gadlus . Just as a person grows physically — born small, without understanding, gradually growing through nursing until he has a child's awareness, then growing further until at five he has understanding to study Scripture ( "at five — Scripture" ), continuing to grow in understanding — so too in Hashem's service: one must constantly labor until one merits leaving mochin d'katnus for mochin d'gadlus — breaking all cravings and evil traits (= mochin d'katnus ) and engaging in His service, thereby knowing Him with mochin d'gadlus . This is man's essential work all his life. Tefilas HaMinchah is exceedingly lofty and the Sages warned about it especially. At Shacharis : mochin d'gadlus . At night: mochin d'katnus (= the darkness of night from contracted da'as ). Light and darkness are da'as and folly — mochin d'gadlus and mochin d'katnus . Day and night are the great luminary and the small luminary: "the great luminary to rule the day, the small luminary..." (= gadlus and katnus ). All judgments derive from mochin d'katnus (= darkness), where the evil inclination and all cravings take hold. Immediately after midday, as the evening shadows incline, the root of mochin d'katnus begins. The essential sweetening is specifically there — sweetening the mochin d'katnus at the very root of their initial hold (for "judgment is sweetened only at its root" ). This is Tefilas HaMinchah — the Sages warned greatly. Though the essential rule of judgments is at night, the essential work is at Minchah time specifically — when the day is still great but has begun inclining toward night. Then is the essential sweetening: at the initial root of mochin d'katnus 's hold (after midday, when night's hold begins). Minchah Gedolah and Minchah Ketanah hint that Minchah encompasses both gadlus and katnus — it is still day ( mochin d'gadlus ) yet mochin d'katnus (= night) has begun stirring. The essential sweetening in completeness is when one merits sweetening them at their supreme root — where all mochin d'gadlus and d'katnus are encompassed together. Below, in the six directions, there is gadlus and katnus ; but high above, at the supreme root of the mochin , there is no gadlus or katnus at all — there the essential sweetening is complete. As understood from Rabbainu's teaching " Chadi Rabbi Shimon " ( LM I:61 ): there is sweetening through the particular intellect belonging to each judgment, but the essential sweetening is through the seichel hakolail [the all-encompassing intellect] — the supreme root of the mochin , where all mochin are encompassed together (all is one), from which the essential sweetening comes. This supreme intellect above all mochin — the world cannot comprehend it; only one who merits it. There is the essential anavah : "in the place of His greatness, there you find His humility." Humility (which to our understanding is katnus — smallness in one's own eyes) and gadlus are one — in the place of His greatness, there specifically you find humility. This cannot be understood except by one who merits it. This is the perfection of true humility that Moshe Rabbainu alav hashalom achieved — able to write of himself all his great praises, and he wrote: "the man Moshe was exceedingly humble" — yet was truly humble, encompassed in the Ain [Nothingness] where greatness and humility are one: "in the place of His greatness, there you find His humility." Not everyone merits humility —

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 6
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 6 (§§ 1–13) Based on LM II:71 ( Chavalim Naflu Li BaN'imim ) Introduction — The No'am , Kavod , Chovlim and N'imim Based on the teaching " Chavalim Naflu Li BaN'imim " ( LM II:71 ). See there. The principle: all of Creation is solely for His glory [ kavod ]. Therefore kavod is the root of all Creation — the root of all the Ten Utterances by which the world was created. When honor comes to a person, he must be very careful not to take any of it for himself — he must elevate all the kavod to Hashem. He must understand from which Utterance this kavod was generated. The essential kavod is through man (= the purpose of all Creation), who was created to magnify and publicize His kavod . Through procreation [ holadah ] — more people being born — His kavod is revealed further. The essential holadah is through the No'am HaElyon [the Supernal Pleasantness], the supreme root of procreation. The No'am HaElyon flows constantly, but a vessel [ k'li ] is needed to receive it — made through tzedakah (to receive the flames of love flowing from the No'am HaElyon ). There is tzedakah of Eretz Yisrael and tzedakah of outside the Land. The essential one is the tzedakah of Eretz Yisrael — the mochin of Eretz Yisrael are in the aspect of no'am : "they delight each other in halachah " (= shalom ). Outside the Land is the aspect of chovlim [those who wound/injure] — the mochin of outside the Land are machaloikes [dispute]: "they wound each other in halachah ." When the No'am HaElyon flows (for holadah through the vessel of tzedakah ), the chovlim (= mochin of outside the Land) fall into the n'imim [the pleasant ones] (= mochin of Eretz Yisrael) to be repaired (that being their time of tikun — their essential corruption came through flawed kavod ). But sometimes the chovlim are so damaged they cannot be repaired — rather, they cause damage to the n'imim as well. From this comes the machaloikes that exists even in Eretz Yisrael. The n'imim themselves are the aspect of shalom — dispute comes only from the damaged chovlim falling among them, and when too corrupt, they damage the n'imim . All through flawed kavod — all the machaloikes in the world, in Eretz Yisrael and outside, derives from there. § 1 — Three Daily Tefilos : Drawing the No'am ; Tefilah as the Essential Kavod This is the three daily tefilos . The No'am HaElyon must be drawn each day: "in His goodness He renews the act of Creation every day." The essential Creation was through the No'am — revealing His kavod (= the root of Creation). Every day, renewed Creation comes through the No'am HaElyon flowing, drawing Jewish souls — magnifying His kavod , sustaining the world. The world's essential sustenance is through tzedakah and chesed (our Sages say) — tzedakah creates the vessel to receive the No'am , revealing His kavod . Daylight is the essential renewed Creation: Hashem causes the sun to rise each morning and set in the evening. We praise this in Birchos HaMe'oros : "in His goodness He renews the act of Creation every day." Daylight is the radiance of the kavod : "the earth shone from His kavod " — drawn from the mochin of the No'am HaElyon : "sweet [ masok ] is the light" (= pleasantness and sweetness). The mochin are the aspect of daylight: "wisdom's advantage... as the advantage of light over darkness." The essential No'am flows in the morning (= daylight). This is Shacharis established by Avraham — the first to reveal His G-dliness: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth — b'hibaram / b'Avraham " (our Sages). Avraham began drawing the No'am HaElyon (= the holy mochin of Eretz Yisrael) — the essential knowledge of His G-dliness. He engaged in tzedakah and chesed all his days to create the vessel. No'am = the right side, Avraham: "pleasantness at Your right hand forever." He was first to reveal the holiness of Eretz Yisrael (meriting its mochin of no'am ). Therefore Avraham established Shacharis . The complete order of prayer is in the morning: Pesukay D'Zimrah (= "pleasant songster of Israel" — drawing the No'am ); preceded by parshas haKorbanos (= tzedakah , generous heart — receiving the No'am ); then Birchos HaMe'oros and Krias Shma (= drawing the mochin ); then Shemoneh Esrai (= drawing the souls, the mochin further below). Through all this, His kavod is revealed. The essential kavod is through tefilah specifically — when we pray and ask for all our needs, physical and spiritual: "call upon Me in the day of trouble; I shall deliver you, and you shall honor Me." This is the essential kavod . Shemoneh Esrai is higher and more precious than the entire order of prayer — through prayer we demonstrate that Hashem governs the world, watches over every detail, and has the power to change nature. He gave us the power and permission to entreat Him through prayer and supplication — until He turn

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 7 Part1
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 7, Part 1 (§§ 1–16) Based on LM I:49 ( LaShemesh Ohel Bahem ) Introduction Based on the teaching " LaShemesh Ohel Bahem " ( LM I:49 ). See there the entire teaching well. § 1 — Minchah : Sweetening Judgments Through Teshuvah — Turning Bad Thoughts to Good This is the aspect of Tefilas HaMinchah . Then is the essential sweetening of judgments — one must be careful to pray with great kavanah to sweeten the fierce judgments aroused then (as the Zohar states, and as explained in the above teaching on the verse "fine flour for a Minchah " ). Minchah is the aspect of judgments (= Pachad Yitzchak ; Yitzchak established Minchah ). The essential tikun and sweetening is through teshuvah — returning from bad thoughts to good thoughts (for they are the essential yitzarim ). As explained there — tefilah , teshuvah , the ten types of melody, and the Hai that was a Dales are all connected. The essential thing: to overpower bad thoughts and transform them to good. The ohr lahaviyus [fiery light] of a Jew's heart is the aspect of Ohr Ain Sof — infinite, boundless yearning — unable to do any service or draw any quality. One must contract [ tzamtzem ] this enthusiasm until there is a chalal [hollow] in the heart: "my heart is hollow within me." The heart is the axis of all qualities (= the worlds). The essential thing: the wisdom within the heart (= good thoughts). When one thinks bad thoughts, chas v'shalom , the hollow in the heart is blocked up. Therefore: contract the heart's enthusiasm — not too much (that being excessive light from which the Breaking of Vessels came). The enthusiasm must be gradual and measured: "my heart is hollow within me." The essential: overpower bad thoughts with good ones — meriting all good qualities and serving Hashem properly. All to reveal His Malchus — for this, everything was created. § 2 — The Daily Cycle: Arvis , Shacharis , Minchah ; the Poor Man's Prayer All this is Tefilas HaMinchah . Then the beginning of the contraction is aroused (from which all judgments derive) — and must be sweetened through focused prayer (= teshuvah ). The matter of the light's enthusiasm and contraction is replicated in man every day: just as at Creation, the Ohr Ain Sof had no place for creation until He contracted it — the wisdom emerged, producing all worlds — so too man (a portion of G-d from above): in his daily service, he must draw the tikun and sustenance of that day's creation anew. Arvis [evening prayer] is the contraction of light (= darkness: "He placed darkness as His concealment" ). Shacharis is the revelation and drawing of light through the tikun of the contraction — the mochin are drawn (= that day's creation). But after prayer, the mochin depart; only a reshimu [trace] remains. After midday, as the day turns — the beginning of the contraction for the next day's creation stirs. Then "harsh judgment prevails." The Sages established Minchah then, warning greatly: "one should always be careful with Tefilas HaMinchah ." Tremendous exertion is needed: nullifying the bad thoughts from the fierce judgments, drawing good thoughts. This is teshuvah — the essential teshuvah of every person: returning each time from bad thoughts to holy thoughts. Thought is in man's hand at every moment — there lies the essential test and free will. Return in thought from wherever you are to holy thoughts. Even if one's thought strayed terribly — believe that every detachment from evil to good is precious to Hashem: "He knows our inclination." The essential evil inclination is the thoughts. Tefilas HaMinchah is the poor man's offering (= tefilah l'ani ) — through daily business, one is rarely spared flawed thoughts ( "from three things no man is spared daily" ). Minchah is teshuvah : from amid all business, remembering Hashem — overpowering bad thoughts with good (= the tikun of the Hai : "there is no poor man except in da'as " ). When one has mercy on oneself, sees one's poverty, does not despair, and prays — "a prayer for the poor man when he is wrapped [in his distress]" — surrounded, unable to flee right or left, as David cried: "they encompassed me, they surrounded me" — yet overpowers and cries to Hashem: this is Tefilas HaMinchah . Through this — the essential tikun of teshuvah : the Hai returns to its place. All judgments from the contraction are sweetened — revealed that within the contraction itself, Hashem is concealed. The contraction is a great kindness — to reveal His G-dliness and Malchus . "Hashem, He is Elokim " — Elokim (contraction) revealed as Hashem: "there is no place devoid of Him." Said twice — for the ascent of both the upper house [ baisa ila'ah ] and the lower house [ baisa tata'ah ]. § 3 — Eliyahu: "Answer Me" Twice — Fire from Heaven vs. Sorcery; the Tzadik 's Torah from Heaven Eliyahu said: "answer me, Hashem, answer me" —

teachings.title: Likutay Halachos - Tefilas HaMinchah Halachah 7 Part2
teachings.content: Likutay Halachos Orach Chaim 2 - Tefilas Haminchah Halachah Part Likutay Halachos — Orach Chaim, Volume 2 Hilchos Tefilas HaMinchah [Laws of the Afternoon Prayer] Halachah 7, Part 2 (§§ 17–31) Based on LM I:49 ( LaShemesh Ohel Bahem ), continued § 17 — Pesach and the Prohibition of Chametz : Haste from Incomplete Is'arusa d'L'sata Pesach and the prohibition of chametz : Israel left in haste [ chipazon ] because they were not worthy of redemption through is'arusa d'l'sata (which was not yet complete). They were compelled to leave in haste (= the prohibition of chametz ). Even at Sinai — though they had some preparation — they were not yet worthy of such a face-to-face prophetic revelation (the Torah was meant to be given after a thousand generations). Therefore the Adversary provoked them through the Erev Rav — the Golden Calf. One cannot enter baisa ila'ah (perception of G-dliness) except according to the tikun of baisa tata'ah : service, good deeds, overpowering bad thoughts — revealing Malchus through the mouth: "I shall make known Your emunah with my mouth." Na'aseh must precede Nishma . The tikun through the Mishkan (gold, silver, copper = guvanin ila'in [supernal colors]). The essential test and free will centers on guarding the Bris (dependent on thought). Overpowering bad thoughts → revealing Malchus → baisa ila'ah ascends. Flawing this (wanting to perceive without purifying thought) → great corruption → the craving for money [ ta'avas mamon ] overpowers (= idolatry: "gods of silver, gods of gold" ). Money at its root is exceedingly lofty — the light of abundance there is less physicalized than that drawn for procreation (which is clothed in the body's seed, where the greatest provocation lies). Sin in forbidden areas damages baisa tata'ah , which then damages the guvanin ila'in (= baisa ila'ah ), leading to idolatry or excessive craving for money (= the Golden Calf).
